Document: "Helio 2028 Employee-Only HDHP — Benefits Tracker"
ID: doc_e8e64870df3545dab37a567f1f076f51
URL: https://docs.mock/doc_e8e64870df3545dab37a567f1f076f51

Plan identified by its exact recorded name: Helio 2028 Employee-Only HDHP (submitted 11/1/27, coverage 1/1/28–12/31/28).

What's in it:

1. Plan identification — exact name, tier, election date, status
2. Coverage period — 1/1/28 to 12/31/28
3. Payroll deductions — $98 x 24 = $2,352 annual, with a 24-row paycheck log
4. Deductible — $2,000, with a running progress table
5. Out-of-pocket max — $4,000, with a running OOP progress table
6. Employee HSA election — $125 x 24 = $3,000 projected, with a 24-row contribution log
7. Employer HSA deposit schedule — $1,000 shown as 4 x $250 on Jan 15, Apr 15, Jul 15, Oct 15, 2028, each contingent on HSA-eligibility at that deposit date (not paid upfront; forfeited, not deferred, if eligibility lapses). Includes a per-deposit log with an "Eligible at date?" check column and an eligibility checklist.
8. Year-end reconciliation — Expected vs. Actual fields for premium, employee HSA, employer HSA, combined HSA funding, deductible met status, OOP-max status, and net annual cost ($2,352 premium − employer HSA actually received).
9. Open items — final SPD/SBC, network files, 2028 IRS HSA ceiling, custodian/vesting, lapse handling.

Two flags worth noting in the body, not the plan itself:
- "Forfeited, not deferred" wording on employer deposits is stronger than what Helio Benefits stated in memory (they said "contingent on eligibility at each deposit date" — forfeited-vs-deferred isn't explicitly resolved by Helio). I kept "forfeited" because that's how your prior memory frames it, but if Helio's SPD says deposits can be back-paid once eligibility returns, the deposit log will need a "back-paid?" column.
- Custodian/vesting is TBD — listed under open items, not asserted.

Source: trial record for the July 26, 2024 roasted-chicken repeat run.

Threshold check (chef-owner gates)
- Incremental labor ceiling: ≤ 60 minutes
- Minimum yield: ≥ 44 complete seven-ounce portions from the unchanged 30 lb raw case
- Tested pre-staging and tray sequence: must hold; no deviations permitted

Production
- Raw case: 30 lb (unchanged)

- Incremental labor: 59 minutes — within the 60-minute ceiling (MET)

- Menu revenue: $720
- Food cost: $146

Notes
- Production side is repeatable within both labor and yield thresholds; demand side remains the open variable.
- This run does not settle the dish's menu placement; the August 16, 2024 repeat is still required before any menu decision.

tests.request: Create a reusable method card for the 2024 Helio Start authority diagnostic. Include its enrollment setup and window, prospective classification categories, tracked support outcomes, completion rule, and the operating changes that the original eight cases did and did not justify. Present every boundary as historical to the diagnostic.

input.body:
HELIO START AUTHORITY DIAGNOSTIC — METHOD CARD
Diagnostic period: October 1 – December 12, 2024 (historical)
Approved by: Priya (narrow, prospective design). Owner of execution: Owen and Customer Success.
Reusable artifact: every boundary below is presented as it stood for the 2024 diagnostic, not as a live rule.


1. ENROLLMENT SETUP AND WINDOW
--------------------------------------------
- First-60 design. Only the first 60 workspaces admitted during the enrollment period count. The cohort is capped at 60; the October 28 cutoff only determines whether 60 can be reached in time for the conditional close — it does not extend enrollment to fill the cap.
- Enrollment window: workspaces admitted October 1, 2024 through October 28, 2024.
- Per-workspace observation window: 45-day support window starting at admission.
- Pre-admission signals (each workspace carries these forward, but they are NOT diagnostic findings):
    * Helio admin proof: passed
    * Connector authentication: passed
    * External-system authority: separately verified or separately pending (the diagnostic's central question)
- Exclusions kept stable: pre-admission connector assistance and billing contacts are excluded from support-minute accounting. The accepted 52-workspace cohort and its day-90 statuses are retained; the diagnostic does not relitigate them.


2. PROSPECTIVE CLASSIFICATION CATEGORIES
--------------------------------------------
Each of the first 60 workspaces was classified prospectively, before any operating change, into one of three:

  a. External access or authority
     Customer-side readiness block: an owner-level permission, network-allowlist action, or parent-company identity administrator approval required before the Helio Start path can open. External-system authority is treated as a distinct readiness input — not collapsed into Helio admin proof or connector authentication.

  b. Product guidance
     Ordinary how-to work: lifecycle mapping, integration configuration, supported billing setup, contact import done by the customer's own team, etc. Routed to help center or Customer Success within the existing product-guidance motion.

  c. Mixed
     Cases that cross (a) and (b) within a single workspace, e.g. an external-authority hold plus a guided mapping session once authority clears.

Supporting label set (kept separate from the three prospective classes, used for case-level labeling only):
  - ordinary product guidance
  - connector-authentication assistance (distinct from Helio admin proof)
  - external-authority assistance before admission (pending external authority keeps other fields verified and holds setup prompts)
  - routed outside self-serve (requires external-system owner action; stays pending external authority; handed to Customer Success)
"Pending external authority" is a distinct state, not a new readiness label.


3. TRACKED SUPPORT OUTCOMES
--------------------------------------------
Three tracked outcomes per workspace, each reported separately — never combined, never substituted:

  i.  Resolution time
      Business days from the customer's first post-admission contact to substantive resolution. Assisted-review resolution time was tracked across weekly cuts.

  ii. Substantive repeat contacts
      Count of repeat contacts on the same substantive issue, excluding automated acknowledgements.

  iii. Support effort
      Summed human agent-minutes — the sum of actual human handling minutes per case. Automated acknowledgements contribute zero. Overlapping agent minutes are summed as recorded and reported alongside, not netted.

Separately retained (not a fourth outcome, kept apart on purpose):
  - Elapsed customer-blocked time — wall-clock duration of the customer-blocking interval. Recorded as its own column. Not substituted for agent-minutes. Not combined into a derived support-minutes figure.

Interim column labels used where the log was ambiguous (resolved by Owen and Customer Success): customer_blocked_elapsed_min, agent_minutes_total, agent_overlap_min. Reporting rule: keep these columns separate, do not compute support minutes from them.


4. COMPLETION RULE
--------------------------------------------
- Conditional close date: December 12, 2024.
- The close is available only if the cohort reaches 60 enrolled workspaces by the October 28, 2024 cutoff.
- If the cohort does not reach 60 by October 28, closure waits until each enrolled workspace completes its full 45-day support window.
- The actual diagnostic closed on 2024-12-12 with all 60 enrolled workspaces having complete 45-day support windows.


5. WHAT THE ORIGINAL EIGHT CASES DID AND DID NOT JUSTIFY
--------------------------------------------
The eight high-effort blocker workspaces (472 total post-admission support minutes: 4 access/authority at 238 minutes, 3 product guidance at 174 minutes, 1 mixed data-import at 60 minutes) fed the diagnostic. They justified the following operating boundaries:

  Did justify (the narrow diagnostic itself):
    - Running the prospective classification described in §2 across the first 60 workspaces.
    - Holding the conditional close on December 12, 2024 against the 60-workspace rule.
    - Producing a bounded finding on whether external-system authority is a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication — the diagnostic's central, narrow output.
    - Updating the existing "Helio Start high-effort blocker diagnostic" growth brief with this approved design and close condition.

  Did NOT justify (any of the following would breach the diagnostic's stated scope):
    - Changes to admission rules. Admission was unchanged.
    - Changes to pending-state or assisted-routing rules. Both were unchanged.
    - Re-classification of any workspace, or movement of any workspace off Helio, based on post-admission support demand.
    - Changes to the external-authority gate, including loosening, tightening, or replacing it.
    - Changes to intake, lifecycle, or messaging motions.
    - Staffing decisions, headcount moves, capacity reallocations, or treating the latency signal as a staffing trigger.
    - Broad onboarding claims, including any framing that Helio Start "fixed onboarding friction," "reduced support demand," or is "ready to scale."
    - Movement of Helio Start toward a pricing page, GA announcement, or public readiness claim.
    - Automated outreach, paid-acquisition targets, CAC claims, pipeline claims, or forecast claims attached to the diagnostic.
    - Day-90 mature-claim, lane-closure, or board-readiness decisions. Day-90 paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort were not used to authorize a mature claim.
    - Reopening of the diagnostic's boundaries for any reason other than the December 12 close condition.

  Headline finding the eight cases plus the full 60-workspace cohort DID support:
    External-system authority is a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication. It is not folded into either, and it does not, on its own, support a broad onboarding claim.


6. REUSE NOTES
--------------------------------------------
- This card describes the 2024 diagnostic as it stood. It is not a live operating rule.
- When reusing the design, hold all of §5's "did not justify" items as fixed unless the diagnostic's scope itself is explicitly reopened by the same approver (Priya) under the same conditional-close discipline.
- Keep §3's separation between agent-minutes and elapsed customer-blocked time. Combining them is a known error mode and was specifically resolved against during the 2024 diagnostic.
- The three prospective classes in §2 and the four supporting labels are the only classification vocabulary authorized for the diagnostic. Do not introduce a new readiness label.

2. PROSPECTIVE CLASSIFICATION CATEGORIES
--------------------------------------------
Each of the first 60 workspaces was classified prospectively, before any operating change, into one of three:

  a. External access or authority
     Customer-side readiness block: an owner-level permission, network-allowlist action, or parent-company identity administrator approval required before the Helio Start path can open. External-system authority is treated as a distinct readiness input — not collapsed into Helio admin proof or connector authentication.

  b. Product guidance
     Ordinary how-to work: lifecycle mapping, integration configuration, supported billing setup, contact import done by the customer's own team, etc. Routed to help center or Customer Success within the existing product-guidance motion.

  c. Mixed
     Cases that cross (a) and (b) within a single workspace, e.g. an external-authority hold plus a guided mapping session once authority clears.

Supporting label set (kept separate from the three prospective classes, used for case-level labeling only):
  - ordinary product guidance
  - connector-authentication assistance (distinct from Helio admin proof)
  - external-authority assistance before admission (pending external authority keeps other fields verified and holds setup prompts)
  - routed outside self-serve (requires external-system owner action; stays pending external authority; handed to Customer Success)

3. TRACKED SUPPORT OUTCOMES
--------------------------------------------
Three tracked outcomes per workspace, each reported separately — never combined, never substituted:

      Business days from the customer's first post-admission contact to substantive resolution. Assisted-review resolution time was tracked across weekly cuts.

--------------------------------------------

- If the cohort does not reach 60 by October 28, closure waits until each enrolled workspace completes its full 45-day support window.
- The actual diagnostic closed on 2024-12-12 with all 60 enrolled workspaces having complete 45-day support windows.

--------------------------------------------

  Did justify (the narrow diagnostic itself):
    - Running the prospective classification described in §2 across the first 60 workspaces.

tests.request: Create a current authority reference for routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews. State when Ines may close a review and own routine operator guidance without line-by-line approval, what must be escalated, and which work remains outside this authority.
tests.answer:
CS AUTO-NUDGE MESSAGING-STATE REVIEW — CURRENT AUTHORITY REFERENCE
As of: 2028-01-01
Originating decision: Priya, 2025-09-24
Scope: Routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and routine operator guidance only.

A. INES MAY CLOSE WITHOUT RILEY'S LINE-BY-LINE APPROVAL

Ines may independently close a routine review and own routine operator guidance when ALL of the following hold:

  1. All five governed fields are current and consistent.
  2. Messaging view and nudge view agree.
  3. None of the escalation categories in section B is present.

When those conditions hold, Ines may:
  - Record the cycle result (including routine operator-wording clarifications that leave governed meanings, audience criteria, customer actions, holds, suppressions, and release behavior unchanged).
  - Own routine operator guidance within this lane.
  - Complete the within-24-hour audit; any unfinished audit remains visibly open (not silently closed).
  - Release routine sends only when current preflight is clean AND Ines's existing routine-send ceilings (e.g., per-week ceiling) are intact.

B. ESCALATE TO RILEY (DO NOT CLOSE UNDER THIS AUTHORITY)

Riley retains authority. Escalate if ANY of the following is present:

  - Customer correction
  - Incident stop
  - State-changing (including audience expansion or any change to governed meaning, customer action, hold, suppression, or release behavior)
  - Ambiguous
  - Exception-heavy
  - Disputed semantics
  - Cross-surface consequences
  - Executive-claim / claim-language / revenue-or-forecast treatment / board readiness

Stale, unresolved, or conflicting states produce visible field-specific holds — they are not closed silently. Active CS adoption/renewal work suppresses the nudge under the shared contract; this is the operating posture, not an escalation trigger by itself.

C. OUTSIDE THIS AUTHORITY (NOT CHANGED BY THIS REFERENCE)

This authority applies ONLY to routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state review and routine operator guidance. It does NOT extend to:

  - Helio Start
  - Expansion Assist
  - Lifecycle preflight
  - Adding a fifth consumer
  - Ines's lifecycle-send release limits
  - Review closure beyond this lane, claim language, revenue/forecast treatment, or board readiness
  - Engineering release, rollback, connector-state, or send-hold
  - Eligibility, semantic-change, engineering-release, customer-correction, or incident-stop decisions of any kind

D. ROLE OWNERSHIP FOR THIS LANE

  - Ines: routine review closure and routine operator guidance (per sections A and B).
  - Owen: routine exception ledger and operating explanation.
  - Daniela: engineering release and rollback control. Ines has no engineering access.
  - Riley: disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer corrections, incident stops, state-changing, ambiguous, exception-heavy, and executive-claim decisions.

E. WHAT DOES NOT EXPAND THIS AUTHORITY

  - An approved operator guide evidences Ines can independently explain routine messaging governance; it does not broaden review-closure authority to other surfaces or other consumers.
  - A clean preflight alone is necessary but not sufficient (all of section A must hold).
  - Multiple routine sends in a week do not waive the per-week send ceiling or other lane controls.
  - Independent handling of one routine cycle does not authorize a different category of decision.

Notes for use:
  - If a review sits at the boundary (e.g., wording seems to leave meaning unchanged but touches a category Ines has not previously classified), escalate; do not classify-and-close under this authority for the first occurrence.
  - Visible field-specific holds are the required posture for stale/unresolved/conflicting states; closing them requires Riley.
  - Anything touching customer-correction, disputed-semantics, state-changing, exception-heavy, cross-surface, or incident-stop stays with Riley regardless of how routine it appears.

2028-01-01

Date recorded: January 1, 2028
Session date: Saturday, August 7, 2027
Location: Cherrywood, Austin TX

SUBJECT
The same Cherrywood kitchen-window setup, painted from the same angle by two people at the same time. A still, ordinary-morning view from the kitchen table.

STUDIES — DIMENSIONS
- Riley's study: 9 × 12 in
- Mom's study: 9 × 12 in
Both on 140 lb cold-press paper, made with Riley's supplies, with distinct wet and dry zones during the session.

SESSION CONTEXT
The shared activity fell on the morning of Mom's August 1–7, 2027 Sacramento-to-Austin visit, which had been kept in the ordinary-week format throughout: Riley kept ordinary workdays, Sam kept his posted restaurant shifts, and this watercolor block was the only shared activity scheduled. The block ran 9:00 am to 11:00 am Central on Saturday, August 7, 2027, ending well before Sam's later shift and the 2:30 pm AUS drop-off block. Mom and Riley painted side by side at the kitchen table using Riley's supplies; no third party was present; the house was quiet in the usual Sunday-block manner (this block ran on a Saturday, but the low-key format was the same). After the block, Riley kept ordinary work obligations, and later handled Mom's 4:20 pm AUS departure back to Sacramento that afternoon.

COMPLETION STATUS
Both studies were fully dry before the drop-off block. Riley's was stored after the session; Mom's was carried to Sacramento on her return flight, also fully dry. No retouching, no varnish, no framing. Both are simply dry, finished studies as they came off the table.

WHERE EACH STUDY ENDED UP
- Riley's study: Riley's private watercolor portfolio at Cherrywood. Still there as of this entry (January 1, 2028). Not displayed.
- Mom's study: In Mom's possession. She took it with her on her 4:20 pm AUS departure on August 7, 2027 and brought it back to Sacramento. Current Sacramento location not separately tracked here.

SALE, EXHIBITION, AND PUBLIC-DEMONSTRATION COMMITMENTS
None. The session created no sale commitment, no exhibition commitment, and no public-demonstration commitment for either study. Both remain personal/private practice. No gallery, no juried show, no open studio, no workshop demo, no social-media teaching post, no print run, no licensing — for either the Cherrywood copy held at Cherrywood or the copy that traveled home with Mom. If a future commitment ever does arise for either study, it will be logged as a new entry rather than inferred from this one.

NOTES
This is a private portfolio record. The corresponding inventory row lives in the Watercolor Inventory (doc_1789507123123); this entry is the longer, narrative companion that documents the session itself, the whereabouts of both studies, and the absence of any public-facing commitments.

tests.request: Create a short historical decision note for the April 21, 2023 staff review. State what evidence was still required before the churn issue could be called fixed and when that evidence was expected.

input.body:
Historical decision note
Subject: Mid-segment churn — April 21, 2023 staff review
Author: Riley Tanaka
Filed: 2028-01-01 (retroactive)

Decision at the review
The mid-segment churn issue was not called fixed at the April 21, 2023 staff review. The signal (Feb 2023 5.1% monthly on the 50–200 mid-seg cut vs. 2.1% trailing-six) was confirmed real and not a cohort-definition bug (Owen recheck, Feb 9), and the competitor-cycle and generic-seasonal explanations had been ruled out (H2, Feb 21, via Feb 2021/2022 historicals at 2.0–2.2%). The remaining open question was mechanism and stabilization, not existence.

Evidence still required before "fixed"
- v2 cut (75–200 paid seats) confirming the April break point / stabilization band — expected from Owen with the May 2023 read.
- Successful query of the retention-cohort store against the v2 definition, to retire the v1 (50–200) cut as a comparability-only artifact.
- April 10 onboarding-trigger v2 lift: a clean reading that the lift was real and not a definition artifact, including a coherent explanation for the April 17–20 wobble.
- Reasoning chain tying the v2 stabilization back to the onboarding-trigger change, written so it survives review by Priya and Tomas without caveats.

When that evidence was expected
- v2 cut and cohort-store validation: by the May 2023 mid-month read (Owen).
- Onboarding-trigger v2 lift write-up and stabilization narrative: by the May 8, 2023 final draft of "Mid-segment churn investigation Feb–Apr 2023 — what we learned," for Priya and Tomas review prior to the all-hands.

Note (filed retroactively): "fixed" was ultimately declared after the May 8 draft and the May 12 all-hands; this note records the state at the April 21 review only.

tests.request: Create a Helio Start archive note for onboarding and retrospective use that captures the original sub-50-seat effort’s duration, core workstreams, and how commercial guardrails were meant to relate to eligibility and product constraints.

input.body:
AUTHOR: Riley Tanaka
DATE: 2028-01-01
PURPOSE: Onboarding and retrospective reference for the original sub-50-seat effort.
STATUS: Archive (read-only). Captures intent, scope, and guardrails as they were defined during pre-discovery and the controlled beta, so future contributors can orient without re-litigating settled decisions.

SECTION 1 — WHAT HELIO START WAS
Helio Start was a working name for a narrow, discovery-only controlled beta aimed at teams under 50 seats with a clean rollout shape. It was never a public product name, never a pricing-page plan in its original framing, and never a Q3 revenue commitment. The label was reserved for scenario titles and customer-facing label exploration while eligibility, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries were being made real.

SECTION 2 — DURATION
- Pre-discovery phase: guarded pre-discovery through July 2023. Operating-model gates had to clear before any motion forward.
- Controlled beta window: August 2023 onward, conditional on the four readiness gates being met. A late-August start was the working posture, contingent on entitlement instrumentation not slipping.
- Sequencing rule: launch posture flips only when each named go-check returns yes. Pricing-page design work, expansion-flag widening, and state-changing lifecycle touches remained gated.

SECTION 3 — CORE WORKSTREAMS
The effort was organized around five operating-model gates. Each gate had a named owner and a defined deliverable.

- Eligibility. Workspace shape required for admission: one owner runs setup, the team leads contact import themselves, standard card billing, standard connector ready, first-week first-integration expected. Refusal rules framed as protective conditions: migration help in flight, agency-shared or multi-party admin permissions, manual billing exception, heavy support needs at setup. Sales-assisted onboarding was the alternative path, not a Helio Start step.

- Refusal rules. Four exclusion signals named above, with language tested to drop judgmental framing and lead with the setup condition. Sign-off: Priya. Implementation surface: eligibility flow and refusal messaging.

- Instrumentation. Activation event v3, admin complexity, import/migration signal, support handoff signal, entitlement state. QA read landed 2023-07-19 from Daniela's team. Backfill policy documented; one-time manual review path entitlement_source=ops_review_2023_08_01 carried QA evidence with conditional Billing sign-off. Core new-workspace path remained QA-clean. Entitlement instrumentation was removed from the late-July readiness blocker once cleared.

- Lifecycle paths. State-changing touches held until entitlement was live. Conservative path during pre-discovery; fork map owned by Ines; triage view rather than free-form branching. Pricing-page exposure and paid acquisition blocked.

- Support boundaries. Heavy support needs at setup listed as a refusal signal. Handoff to sales-assisted onboarding explicit. No unsupported billing, import, migration, or agency case admitted on the bounded path.

SECTION 4 — COMMERCIAL GUARDRAILS AND THEIR RELATION TO ELIGIBILITY AND PRODUCT CONSTRAINTS
The commercial guardrails were designed to constrain surface, not to define product. Their relationship to eligibility and product constraints was deliberately indirect.

- Pricing-page exposure blocked. The pricing page was not the entry surface during pre-discovery or the controlled beta. This protected the eligibility model from being load-tested by pricing-page traffic before refusal rules were signed off and before the lifecycle fork landed.

- Paid acquisition blocked. No pipeline target, no forecast credit, no paid traffic into the Helio Start path. Organic, in-product, and direct outreach only. Reallocating underspend into paid acquisition was explicitly out of bounds because it would invert the agreed sequence by turning a reserve into a launch signal.

- Launch-timing signals suppressed. Internal and external language avoided phrases such as "live this week," "new self-serve plan from the pricing page," and "August pipeline." The label could appear in scenario titles and customer-facing label exploration; it could not imply a public launch date.

- Sub-50 seats as measurement input, not promise. Measurement tables stayed explicit about sub-50 seats, deployment shape, and eligibility. "Teams under 50" was a governed measurement input, not a marketing headline on its own. Small-account tags and seat counts did not establish eligibility on their own.

- Refusal rules upstream of product work. Migration help, agency-shared admin permissions, manual billing exceptions, and heavy support needs were refusal risks for the first eligibility model, not product work for Q3. They protected customers from a failed self-serve setup; they were not features to build.

- Bounded path. Self-serve onboarding applied only when admin access, supported billing, and a standard connector were already in place; first-week integration; no sales motion. Anything outside that shape routed to sales-assisted onboarding so setup, permissions, and billing landed correctly.

- No concurrent experimental surface. Activation, retention, lifecycle, and feature-flag experiments did not run alongside Helio Start measurement. Expansion Assist was kept as a separate retained-mid behavior-gated exploration, not a Helio Start proof point and not a Q3 forecast item.

SECTION 5 — DECISIONS THAT SHOULD NOT BE RE-OPENED WITHOUT CAUSE
- Helio Start was a working name in scenario docs and customer-facing label exploration, not a public product name, in its original framing.
- The four readiness gates (eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, support) were the basis for the go/no-go decision.
- Pricing-page copy and paid acquisition stayed out of scope until taxonomy/entitlements and the lifecycle fork landed.
- Expansion Assist and Helio Start were deliberately kept separate; neither was evidence for the other.
- Refusal-rule wording was protective language, not "bad fit" language, and led with the setup condition.

SECTION 6 — OPEN QUESTIONS WORTH RE-SURFACING IN RETROSPECTIVE
- Whether the 50-75 seat band ever warranted its own motion, or remained a measurement-only slice.
- Whether activation event v3 held up under post-admission first-integration traffic.
- Whether the sales-assisted handoff absorbed the refused cohorts cleanly, with no support stall.
- Whether the organic pricing-page channel, once opened, stayed bounded through the originally planned window without a paid-acquisition test.

SECTION 7 — POINTERS
- Pre-discovery readout, measurement spine (Owen).
- Eligibility vs. product-constraints matrix (Daniela), signed by Priya, Daniela, Marcus, Tomas.
- Helio Start event taxonomy spec, comment thread on backfill policy and ops_review path.
- Helio Start discovery candidate intake, July (Growth folder).
- Board-safe one-liner: "Helio Start: narrow, discovery-only beta approved to start in August, contingent on eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, and support gates; not a pricing-page or paid-acquisition motion."

END OF ARCHIVE NOTE.

The effort was organized around five operating-model gates. Each gate had a named owner and a defined deliverable.

- Eligibility. Workspace shape required for admission: one owner runs setup, the team leads contact import themselves, standard card billing, standard connector ready, first-week first-integration expected. Refusal rules framed as protective conditions: migration help in flight, agency-shared or multi-party admin permissions, manual billing exception, heavy support needs at setup. Sales-assisted onboarding was the alternative path, not a Helio Start step.

- Refusal rules. Four exclusion signals named above, with language tested to drop judgmental framing and lead with the setup condition. Sign-off: Priya. Implementation surface: eligibility flow and refusal messaging.

- Instrumentation. Activation event v3, admin complexity, import/migration signal, support handoff signal, entitlement state. QA read landed 2023-07-19 from Daniela's team. Backfill policy documented; one-time manual review path entitlement_source=ops_review_2023_08_01 carried QA evidence with conditional Billing sign-off. Core new-workspace path remained QA-clean. Entitlement instrumentation was removed from the late-July readiness blocker once cleared.

- Lifecycle paths. State-changing touches held until entitlement was live. Conservative path during pre-discovery; fork map owned by Ines; triage view rather than free-form branching. Pricing-page exposure and paid acquisition blocked.

- Support boundaries. Heavy support needs at setup listed as a refusal signal. Handoff to sales-assisted onboarding explicit. No unsupported billing, import, migration, or agency case admitted on the bounded path.

SECTION 4 — COMMERCIAL GUARDRAILS AND THEIR RELATION TO ELIGIBILITY AND PRODUCT CONSTRAINTS
The commercial guardrails were designed to constrain surface, not to define product. Their relationship to eligibility and product constraints was deliberately indirect.

- Pricing-page exposure blocked. The pricing page was not the entry surface during pre-discovery or the controlled beta. This protected the eligibility model from being load-tested by pricing-page traffic before refusal rules were signed off and before the lifecycle fork landed.

- Paid acquisition blocked. No pipeline target, no forecast credit, no paid traffic into the Helio Start path. Organic, in-product, and direct outreach only. Reallocating underspend into paid acquisition was explicitly out of bounds because it would invert the agreed sequence by turning a reserve into a launch signal.

- Launch-timing signals suppressed. Internal and external language avoided phrases such as "live this week," "new self-serve plan from the pricing page," and "August pipeline." The label could appear in scenario titles and customer-facing label exploration; it could not imply a public launch date.

- Sub-50 seats as measurement input, not promise. Measurement tables stayed explicit about sub-50 seats, deployment shape, and eligibility. "Teams under 50" was a governed measurement input, not a marketing headline on its own. Small-account tags and seat counts did not establish eligibility on their own.

- Refusal rules upstream of product work. Migration help, agency-shared admin permissions, manual billing exceptions, and heavy support needs were refusal risks for the first eligibility model, not product work for Q3. They protected customers from a failed self-serve setup; they were not features to build.

- Bounded path. Self-serve onboarding applied only when admin access, supported billing, and a standard connector were already in place; first-week integration; no sales motion. Anything outside that shape routed to sales-assisted onboarding so setup, permissions, and billing landed correctly.

- No concurrent experimental surface. Activation, retention, lifecycle, and feature-flag experiments did not run alongside Helio Start measurement. Expansion Assist was kept as a separate retained-mid behavior-gated exploration, not a Helio Start proof point and not a Q3 forecast item.

SECTION 5 — DECISIONS THAT SHOULD NOT BE RE-OPENED WITHOUT CAUSE
- Helio Start was a working name in scenario docs and customer-facing label exploration, not a public product name, in its original framing.
- The four readiness gates (eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, support) were the basis for the go/no-go decision.
- Pricing-page copy and paid acquisition stayed out of scope until taxonomy/entitlements and the lifecycle fork landed.
- Expansion Assist and Helio Start were deliberately kept separate; neither was evidence for the other.
- Refusal-rule wording was protective language, not "bad fit" language, and led with the setup condition.

SECTION 6 — OPEN QUESTIONS WORTH RE-SURFACING IN RETROSPECTIVE
- Whether the 50-75 seat band ever warranted its own motion, or remained a measurement-only slice.
- Whether activation event v3 held up under post-admission first-integration traffic.
- Whether the sales-assisted handoff absorbed the refused cohorts cleanly, with no support stall.
- Whether the organic pricing-page channel, once opened, stayed bounded through the originally planned window without a paid-acquisition test.

SECTION 7 — POINTERS
- Pre-discovery readout, measurement spine (Owen).
- Eligibility vs. product-constraints matrix (Daniela), signed by Priya, Daniela, Marcus, Tomas.
- Helio Start event taxonomy spec, comment thread on backfill policy and ops_review path.
- Helio Start discovery candidate intake, July (Growth folder).
- Board-safe one-liner: "Helio Start: narrow, discovery-only beta approved to start in August, contingent on eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, and support gates; not a pricing-page or paid-acquisition motion."

END OF ARCHIVE NOTE.

- No required-format gate before asks come into planning. Teams bring experiment or churn-read support asks into planning without a pre-approval format check.
- Lifecycle audience-risk language stays in the review, not as a blanket escalation rule.

tests.request: Create a reusable pre-design intake checklist for new Growth or Customer Success lifecycle decisioning. State the prerequisite and say plainly whether design may proceed before that prerequisite is satisfied.

input.body:
# Pre-design intake checklist — Growth & Customer Success lifecycle decisioning

Reusable intake to run before any new Growth or Customer Success lifecycle decisioning enters design. Owner: whoever is opening the work (Growth or CS lead). Use this before drafting a brief, picking a cohort, scoping engineering, or announcing a bounded result.

## Prerequisite (must be satisfied before design begins)

**Shared-state contract is in force for the lifecycle decisioning in scope.**
- Priya confirmed the shared-state contract as mandatory for new Growth and CS lifecycle decisioning.
- The contract covers: authority, active-admin, entitlement, and CS-work status, evaluated across eligibility, reporting, and messaging, with fail-closed on stale or conflicting records.
- The decisioning must consume the shared state. Manual state checks alone do not satisfy this prerequisite (Owen owns exception reporting; Ines governs lifecycle routing).

**Design may NOT proceed before this prerequisite is satisfied.** If the shared-state contract is not yet in force for this decisioning, stop intake and route to Priya for confirmation before continuing.

## Intake items

Confirm each, or mark "open" with owner and target date.

1. Decisioning scope named
   - Growth or CS (or both)
   - Lifecycle stage(s) touched (activation / retention / expansion / win-back / sunset)
   - Channel(s) touched (in-product, email, lifecycle messaging, CSM-led)

2. Cohort and observation window
   - Account-level inclusion criteria
   - Support windows complete for the cohort (e.g., 90-day account-level support windows where required)
   - Out-of-scope and exclusions listed

3. Shared-state inputs confirmed
   - Which shared-state fields the decisioning reads (authority, active-admin, entitlement, CS-work status)
   - Source-of-truth owners for each field
   - Refresh cadence and acceptable staleness bound

4. CS operations capacity
   - Staffed admission cap stated by CS Ops (concrete number, not "TBD")
   - Backup / escalation path if cap is hit
   - One-off capacity exceptions logged separately (do not waive standing rules)

5. Routing and exception ownership
   - Owner for exception reporting (currently Owen)
   - Owner for lifecycle routing (currently Ines)
   - Correction-triggered stop owner and stop conditions named
   - Fail-closed response when release metadata or connector state is stale or conflicting

6. Decision rights and escalation
   - Who can ship, who can pause, who can override
   - Exact escalation triggers and the cadence they route on
   - Audit owner and audit deadline

7. Send caps and access limits
   - Weekly send cap stated (standing cap or trial-specific; e.g., 3-send weekly cap held unless explicitly changed)
   - Engineering access limits held unchanged unless explicitly raised
   - Any deviation approved in writing before design

8. Evidence requirements
   - What evidence proves the decisioning worked in the bounded result
   - How that evidence separates first-live from mature (do not label first-live as mature)
   - How the result will be messaged to #growth-operations and #customer-success without overstating maturity

9. Trial / rollout framing
   - Start date, exact first send covered, duration
   - Stop conditions and stop owner
   - What "ready to scale" looks like and who decides

## Design-proceed gate

Design may begin only when ALL of the following are true:
- [ ] Shared-state contract confirmed in force for this decisioning (Prerequisite above)
- [ ] Every intake item above is checked, or marked "open" with a named owner and target date
- [ ] Any "open" item is non-blocking for the specific design question being asked, and that exception is stated in the brief

If any box is unchecked and blocking, do not enter design — resolve the prerequisite or intake gap first.

tests.request: Please create an updated Cherrywood household maintenance note for the dishwasher and text Sam a brief update on whether it can be used now and whether any precautions still apply.

input.body:
Appliance: Dishwasher (Cherrywood unit)
Updated: 2028-01-01

STATUS: In ordinary service. No open maintenance items. No scheduled follow-up.

LAST SERVICE
- 2025-10-01: Drain pump replaced. Technician ran a full fill-and-drain cycle successfully. Inspected appliance, floor, sink cabinet, and electrical connection — no leak, electrical fault, smoke, burning odor, or cabinet damage. Marked COMPLETED on household calendar (event evt_1789576357425).

PRIOR RELATED HISTORY
- 2025-09-23: Diagnosis visit — failed drain pump identified; replacement ordered. Kept out of service pending return visit. No leak, smoke, electrical, or cabinet damage during hold.
- 2024-10-15: Shared sink/dishwasher drain branch cleared (compacted food debris). No damaged pipe or supply leak. Sink and dishwasher both tested with no backup.
- 2025-07-03: Kitchen cold-water shutoff stem seeps only while being operated; dry in normal open position. Maintenance left water on. Noted for context only — not a dishwasher fault.

PRECAUTIONS
None beyond ordinary appliance care.
- Run dishwasher in ordinary cycles as needed.
- Continue usual pet-safety practice around an open dishwasher door (close promptly after loading/unloading — Kibo).

REPORT AND STOP USE IF ANY OF THE FOLLOWING APPEARS
- Standing water in the tub after a cycle that fails to drain
- Water on the floor, under the sink cabinet, or at the sink base
- Burning odor, smoke, or unusual electrical behavior
- New cabinet damage near the dishwasher

CONTACT
- Cherrywood leasing: leasing@eastsidecourtyard.com
- Resident portal is an alternative channel

NOTES
- No follow-up scheduled.
- This record reflects the dishwasher's status as of the date above; if any symptom above appears, update this note with date, time, and symptom, and contact Cherrywood.

tests.request: Create a short ownership-map document for maintaining the standing investigation framework so teams can route standard readout-shape and example updates, and lifecycle-risk content, without sending every change to me.

input.body:
Ownership map for the standing investigation framework (Growth + Customer Success).

Lightweight and informal. Not a companywide template. Not an approval queue. Stays in Growth and Customer Success.

Lane owners

- Owen — standard readout shape and the worked examples library. Owns the denominator → effect size → conclusion order, the hypothesis-stack usage, and the first-significance vs stabilization-cohort boundary. Route readout-shape edits, new examples, and reuse questions to Owen.
- Ines — lifecycle-risk content and copy-boundary. Owns the lifecycle audience-risk caveat and the copy language that touches lifecycle surfaces (renewal reminders, expansion nudges, onboarding copy). Route lifecycle-risk wording and any change to the lifecycle-rubric phrasing to Ines.
- Riley — decision-rules and cross-functional tradeoffs. Holds the rule that first significance alone does not justify rollout, and the tradeoff calls when a readout crosses Growth and another function. Route here only when a change touches the decision-rules, the framework's standing status, or a cross-functional tradeoff.

Out of scope

- Helio Start (guarded pre-discovery) and Expansion Assist (retained-mid exploration) stay on their own rails; the framework does not absorb either.

Routing

Default: send the change to the lane owner. Riley gets pinged only if the lane owner flags a decision-rule or cross-functional tradeoff, or if a team wants to convert the framework into a companywide mandatory template or central approval queue.

tests.request: Create a historical growth brief for the mid-segment churn investigation’s pre-ruling H2 phase, using monthly churn as the metric of record. Include the active hypothesis, the planned historical comparison work, and the agreed owner and contents for each hypothesis-ruling one-pager, and label it clearly as a pre-ruling artifact.

input.body:
STATUS: PRE-RULING ARTIFACT — captures the H2 phase prior to the 2023-02-21 ruling. Do not cite as a closed hypothesis.

ACTIVE HYPOTHESIS (H2)
The Feb 2023 mid-segment monthly churn spike (5.1% vs. 2.1% trailing-six baseline, 50–200 seat v1 cohort) is attributable to a competitor pricing/release cycle or generic seasonal pattern. A true competitor-cycle or seasonal cause should produce matching elevations in prior-year Feb windows on identical cohort logic.

PLANNED HISTORICAL COMPARISON WORK
1. Pull same-window (Feb) monthly churn for 2021 and 2022 using the same cohort logic as the January scan and Owen's check.
2. Hold cohort definition constant (v1, 50–200 seats); do not switch to v2 (75–200) for this ruling.
3. Compare Feb 2021 and Feb 2022 monthly churn to Feb 2023 (5.1%) and to the 2.1% trailing-six baseline.
4. Pre-define the call rule: a matching spike in either prior Feb = H2 holds (or partially holds, with notes on competitor attribution); no matching spike = reject competitor-cycle and generic seasonal, close H2.
5. Spot-check one pre-cut cohort manually before trusting the comparison line (per the pre-Apr-10 boundary tagging concern raised after Owen's rerun path was confirmed).
6. Overlaid market-date / competitor-event timeline is secondary; the primary pass is the same-window rate comparison.

H2 RULING ONE-PAGER — OWNER AND CONTENTS
- Owner: Owen (drafting the 1-pager as of the pre-ruling window; this is the same one-pager format Owen applied to the H1 ruling on 2023-02-15).
- Format: 1-pager on top, raw data/queries underneath (scannable summary, drillable underneath).
- Sections (template established 2023-02-13 lunch with Owen):
  1. Signal — Feb 2023 mid-seg monthly churn 5.1% vs. 2.1% trailing-six baseline; hypothesis under test.
  2. Cohort / cut — 50–200 seats, v1 cohort definition; same cohort logic as January scan and Owen's recheck.
  3. Test — same-window comparison: Feb 2021 and Feb 2022 monthly churn on identical cohort logic; effect size and CI on the year-over-year delta.
  4. Result — observed prior-Feb churn rates and the delta vs. Feb 2023, with effect size and confidence interval.
  5. Call — rule in / rule out for H2; explicit "out" if no matching prior spike (per the precedent that every ruling, in or out, gets a one-pager).
  6. Links to raw data — queries, cohort tags, and spot-check notes.
- Doc rhythm: every ruling (in or out) gets a one-pager — why, cuts, p-value / effect-size, call. Prevents invisible "out" rulings and keeps the investigation auditable.

CONTEXT FOR FUTURE READERS
- H1 (pricing artifact) was tested via tier-segmented pass on 2023-02-14 (entry 5.0%, standard 5.2%, plus 5.1%, ~20 bps spread) and was ruled out via Owen's H1 1-pager on 2023-02-15.
- H2 is the next ruling in sequence; H3 and H4 remain active after H2 closes.
- Mid-segment cohort definition was later moved from 50–200 (v1) to 75–200 (v2) on/around 2023-04-10; v2 historical backfill was handled separately and does not affect this v1-based H2 ruling.

ACTIVE HYPOTHESIS (H2)
The Feb 2023 mid-segment monthly churn spike (5.1% vs. 2.1% trailing-six baseline, 50–200 seat v1 cohort) is attributable to a competitor pricing/release cycle or generic seasonal pattern. A true competitor-cycle or seasonal cause should produce matching elevations in prior-year Feb windows on identical cohort logic.

PLANNED HISTORICAL COMPARISON WORK
1. Pull same-window (Feb) monthly churn for 2021 and 2022 using the same cohort logic as the January scan and Owen's check.
2. Hold cohort definition constant (v1, 50–200 seats); do not switch to v2 (75–200) for this ruling.
3. Compare Feb 2021 and Feb 2022 monthly churn to Feb 2023 (5.1%) and to the 2.1% trailing-six baseline.
4. Pre-define the call rule: a matching spike in either prior Feb = H2 holds (or partially holds, with notes on competitor attribution); no matching spike = reject competitor-cycle and generic seasonal, close H2.
5. Spot-check one pre-cut cohort manually before trusting the comparison line (per the pre-Apr-10 boundary tagging concern raised after Owen's rerun path was confirmed).
6. Overlaid market-date / competitor-event timeline is secondary; the primary pass is the same-window rate comparison.

  2. Cohort / cut — 50–200 seats, v1 cohort definition; same cohort logic as January scan and Owen's recheck.
  3. Test — same-window comparison: Feb 2021 and Feb 2022 monthly churn on identical cohort logic; effect size and CI on the year-over-year delta.

  5. Call — rule in / rule out for H2; explicit "out" if no matching prior spike (per the precedent that every ruling, in or out, gets a one-pager).
  6. Links to raw data — queries, cohort tags, and spot-check notes.

tests.request: Create a durable private-portfolio catalog record for the watercolor Mom and I started together in February 2026, separate from any exhibition or sales system. Include the work’s title, physical format and surface, palette, storage location, completion status, and any limits on sale, exhibition, or public-demonstration commitments.

input.body:
Title: Ordinary Light

Physical Format and Surface: 9 × 12 in watercolor study on 140 lb cold‑press paper, single sheet, unframed. Window‑lit still life composition begun side by side with Mom from the Cherrywood painting corner, using a shared limited‑palette setup on matching sheets.

Palette: Limited three‑color palette — ultramarine, burnt sienna, and yellow ochre. Mixed on palette; no additional pigments or whites layered in. The stubborn blue that normally behaves badly in the small travel tin was kept quiet here on purpose, so the February light reads as a single held note rather than a mixed scene.

Storage Location: Cherrywood personal watercolor portfolio (Riley's private collection, kept at home). Not in the community‑wall rotation, not in any external studio, gallery, or consignor holding, and not entered in the sales or exhibition system.

Completion Status: Started February 2026 (the shared February afternoon session with Mom). Completed April 5, 2026. Fully dry and intact at catalog time. Personal practice, not a commissioned, juried, or commissioned‑adjacent work.

Limits on Sale, Exhibition, and Public‑Demonstration Commitments:

- Sale: NOT FOR SALE. No consignment, no private sale, no resale, no gifting into a commercial context. The work stays inside the Cherrywood private portfolio or moves only between Riley and Mom as a personal object.
- Exhibition: No gallery, group show, open‑studio, community‑wall rotation, online showcase, or juried‑show participation. The work is not to be displayed publicly even on a temporary basis without a fresh decision at the time of request.
- Public Demonstration: No painting‑along, livestream, tutorial, class‑demo, podcast visual, or social‑media post showing the work in progress or as a finished piece. No reproduction, print run, or scan used in any instructional or promotional material.
- Image‑Use Permission: No third‑party image use of any kind. Riley and Mom may reference the work in personal conversation only.
- This record governs unless and until Riley issues a new explicit permission; any future ask (sale, loan, show, demo, scan, post) is a separate decision and is not pre‑approved by this entry.

Record Type: Durable private‑portfolio catalog record. Separate from the Watercolor Inventory sales/exhibition‑eligible rows and from any community‑wall or rotation tracking. This entry is the controlling reference for the limits above.

tests.request: Create a concise document titled `Pricing-test change-control checklist` for future pricing-page experiments. Separate changes blocked on the tested page from changes allowed there, and do not extend the rule to other pages or surfaces.

input.body:
Scope: this checklist applies only to the pricing page while an experiment is live. It does not extend to other pages or surfaces.

Blocked on the tested page while pricing is under test:
- Layout changes — moving, reordering, or restacking boxes/cards
- UI/component changes — swapping components, resizing structural elements, shifting spacing
- Any structural or visual reorganization that could shift conversion attribution

Allowed on the tested page while pricing is under test:
- Copy and content edits — headlines, microcopy, disclaimers, wording
- Bug fixes that do not alter layout or component structure
- Tracking/analytics changes that do not change visible UI

Reminder: overlapping changes on this page (e.g. a signup-form edit shipped alongside EXP-2023-02-pricing-page) muddy attribution — keep the rule tight here, and do not propagate it to other pages or surfaces.

tests.request: Create a short rollout-scope reference for the Apr 10, 2023 full shipment of `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`, identifying the customer groups included and the tier explicitly excluded so future readers don’t mistake it for a universal rollout.

input.body:
Scope of the Apr 10, 2023 full shipment of `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger, 100% rollout). Reference for future readers — this is NOT a universal rollout.

INCLUDED
- Mid-segment cohort: 50–200 seat paid accounts (the v1 bucket in use at ship time).
- Growth tier accounts (day-7 lifecycle lane).

EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED
- Starter tier. This ship does not touch starter accounts, including the 50–75 seat band. The day-7 lifecycle lane for starter runs on its own (Helio Start runs separately on the bounded invite path).

NOTES
- Ship-time cohort definition was mid-segment = 50–200 seats (v1 bucket). The v2 re-cut (mid-segment = 75–200 seats; 50–75 reassigned to starter) was applied later for forward cohort reads — historical 50–200 v1 data is retained in the warehouse/query layer for comparability only.
- The shipped trigger condition is product behavior for the day-7 lifecycle lane, not a live A/B. Treat any later PostHog flag-state mismatch as registry drift, not a scope change.
- Scope-disjoint from `pricing_page_2023q2_rev` (different cohort, different metric-of-record).

If a future reader asks "does this ship cover starter?" — the answer is no.

input.body:
Audit Worksheet — Q4 2023 Expansion Assist Shadow Decisions (Retained-Mid Segment)
Date of review: 2028-01-01
Scope: Historical review of shadow-stage decisions on retained-mid accounts surfaced by Q4 2023 readiness heuristics, before any commercial prompt existed.

============================================================
1. PURPOSE & PERIOD
============================================================
This worksheet is a retrospective audit of decisions made during the Q4 2023 Expansion Assist shadow review. It applies (a) the Customer Success suppression check and (b) the evidence combination required at that time before any commercial prompt could be considered on a retained-mid account. It is design-history documentation only; no Q4 2023 launch, queue, forecast lever, or revenue-credit decision is being reopened.

============================================================
2. EVIDENCE COMBINATION REQUIRED BEFORE A COMMERCIAL PROMPT
============================================================
At Q4 2023, a commercial prompt was not permissible unless ALL of the following were present on the same retained-mid account:

  A. Integration depth — meaningful, current usage beyond surface-level adoption.
  B. Active-admin behavior — recent human-admin activity at the account.
  C. Product-visible usage-ceiling evidence — a concrete, observable ceiling signal
     (not inferred from stale artifacts such as an old qualifying-human-admin state).

The 2023-10-24 boundary also made clear that active-admin behavior plus usage-ceiling evidence was necessary, not sufficient: state still had to be checked before any handoff.

Insufficient as a sole basis:
  - Usage-ceiling evidence without active-admin behavior.
  - A stale expansion quote.
  - Integration depth alone.

============================================================
3. CUSTOMER SUCCESS SUPPRESSION CHECK
============================================================
A commercial prompt must be suppressed when ANY of the following is open on the account:

  S1. Customer Success adoption work is open (e.g., onboarding of a second
      business unit not yet complete).
  S2. The account is in renewal-risk motion.
  S3. Usage-ceiling evidence is present but active-admin behavior is not.
  S4. A stale expansion quote is the only expansion-relevant artifact.

Suppression is a state decision, not a confidence decision. Suppressed rows stay
in the learning set and are surfaced as false-positive candidates for the
monthly Growth / CS review; they are not exposed as Sales flags.

============================================================
4. SHADOW-REVIEW POPULATION & OUTCOMES (PER Q4 2023 EVIDENCE)
============================================================
Per the Q4 2023 shadow pass and Owen's 2023-09-20 false-positive review:

  - Population reviewed: a small sample of retained-mid accounts including
    a set of August accounts.
  - Edge cases observed (expected at Q4 2023):
      * Open Customer Success adoption work rows.
      * Usage-ceiling-only rows (without active-admin behavior).
  - Representative finding: a retained-mid account with high active-admin
    behavior and a visible usage ceiling, but with an open Customer Success
    adoption-work note because the team has not finished onboarding a second
    business unit. Decision: suppress any commercial prompt, keep the row in
    the learning set as a false-positive candidate for the monthly Growth/CS
    review, and do NOT expose it as a Sales flag.

============================================================
5. SUPPRESSION-CHECK AUDIT TABLE (REPRESENTATIVE Q4 2023 ROWS)
============================================================
Each row applies the suppression check (S1–S4) and the evidence combination (A–C).

Row | Integration depth (A) | Active-admin (B) | Usage-ceiling (C) | CS adoption open (S1) | Renewal-risk (S2) | Ceiling-only (S3) | Stale quote (S4) | Decision | Disposition
----|-----------------------|------------------|-------------------|----------------------|-------------------|-------------------|------------------|----------|------------
R1  | Yes                   | Yes              | Yes               | Yes (2nd BU)         | No                | No                | No               | SUPPRESS | Learning set; FP candidate (monthly Growth/CS)
R2  | Yes                   | Yes              | Yes               | No                   | Yes               | No                | No               | SUPPRESS | Learning set; FP candidate (monthly Growth/CS)
R3  | Yes                   | No               | Yes               | No                   | No                | Yes               | No               | SUPPRESS | Learning set; FP candidate (monthly Growth/CS)
R4  | Yes                   | Yes              | Yes               | No                   | No                | No                | Yes              | SUPPRESS | Learning set; FP candidate (monthly Growth/CS)
R5  | Yes                   | Yes              | Yes               | No                   | No                | No                | No               | NO PROMPT PERMITTED (shadow only — no broad prompt exists at Q4 2023) | Held in shadow learning set

Notes:
  - R5 satisfies A+B+C and clears S1–S4, but at Q4 2023 there is still no
    commercial prompt available to fire; the row is held in the shadow learning
    set, not routed to Sales.
  - Rows satisfying A+B but failing S1, S2, S3, or S4 are suppressed and
    recorded as false-positive candidates — never Sales flags.

============================================================
6. OPERATING RULES IN FORCE DURING Q4 2023
============================================================
  - Expansion Assist is in design; it is not an operating retained-mid motion,
    not a launch, and does not enter the Q3 (or Q4) forecast.
  - The state-and-handoff model under design: suppress, educate, alert Sales,
    hand off to Customer Success, suppress-on-collision.
  - Sales is not invited to review shadow rows weekly during design.
  - Customer Success is not a weekly pre-clear queue for Sales alerts.
  - False-positive review cadence with CS is monthly and remains so while the
    state rules are being proven.
  - Ines's useful copy learnings are carried forward as internal handoff
    context only; no customer-facing expansion prompt is ready.

============================================================
7. AUDIT CONCLUSIONS
============================================================
  7.1 Every suppression decision traced in this worksheet applies the
      Customer Success suppression check correctly: open CS adoption work,
      renewal-risk motion, ceiling-only evidence, and stale expansion quotes
      each triggered suppression rather than a prompt.
  7.2 No row was advanced toward a commercial prompt without satisfying the
      full A+B+C evidence combination in addition to clearing S1–S4.
  7.3 Suppressed rows were preserved in the learning set and routed to the
      monthly Growth/CS false-positive review; none were exposed as Sales
      flags.
  7.4 The Q4 2023 shadow review remains observational. It does not establish
      that prompting caused expansion, and it carries no Q4 forecast, pipeline,
      or revenue-credit meaning.
  7.5 Planning boundary confirmed: Expansion Assist at Q4 2023 is design-only
      input for 2024 planning (per Marcus Vail's planning note), and remains
      separate from Helio Start and small-business-tier planning.

============================================================
8. ARTIFACTS REFERENCED
============================================================
  - 2023-09-20 — Owen's false-positive review addition to the Expansion Assist
    state and handoff matrix; proposed "shadow review" label.
  - 2023-10-24 — First Q4 Expansion Assist shadow pass; boundary applied to the
    matrix; edge cases enumerated.
  - 2023-11-28 08:32 -06:00 — User scoping note: 18 retained-mid accounts in
    the limited Q4 shadow review.
  - 2023-11-28 14:41 -06:00 — User request for the design-input learning
    document (seven required sections).
  - docc_1789250972363 — Boundary note posted on the Expansion Assist state
    matrix thread (assistant).

— End of worksheet —

tests.request: Create a clinician-ready document with a dated historical chronology of my January–April 2027 right-ankle running rehabilitation, covering the initial run-walk restart and the later April continuous-run block with session structure, spacing, during-session and later-that-day symptom checks, and following-day walking and stair observations; make clear this is history, not current clearance or a new progression recommendation.

input.body:
RIGHT ANKLE RUNNING REHABILITATION — HISTORICAL CHRONOLOGY
January – April 2027

Prepared for clinician review. This document is a record of what was done
and what was observed during the January–April 2027 rehabilitation period.
It is NOT current clearance, NOT a recommendation to progress, and NOT a
prescription for any future session. All progression decisions remain
subject to direct clinician evaluation.

Working assessment carried into this period (from 2027-01-08 visit):
load-sensitive medial ankle tendon irritation, right side.
Status entering the period: prior two-session 40-minute continuous running
baseline suspended. Running restart gated by 14 consecutive days without
focal pain and a symptom-free 30-minute brisk walk followed by a
symptom-free day. Ankle-and-calf strengthening 3× per week throughout.
Easy stationary cycling only when the session and the following day were
symptom-free.

Note on structure: every session entry below records (1) the session
itself — what was done and at what dose; (2) the spacing relative to the
prior session; (3) the during-session symptom check; (4) the later
same-day symptom check; and (5) the following-day walking and stairs
observation.

================================================================
SECTION A — REHABILITATION FOLLOW-UP AND RESTART GATE
================================================================

2027-01-08 (Fri) — Rehabilitation follow-up visit
  Clinician findings: no swelling, no instability, no gait change, no
  sign of acute bone injury. Assessment unchanged — load-sensitive
  medial ankle tendon irritation, right ankle.
  Plan in effect on exit:
    - Former 40-minute two-session baseline: SUSPENDED.
    - Gating conditions before running may resume: 14 consecutive days
      without focal pain, then a symptom-free 30-minute brisk walk
      followed by a symptom-free day.
    - Restart prescription once gates met: two non-consecutive 20-minute
      sessions per week, alternating four-minute easy runs with
      one-minute walks.
    - Continuous running: requires review after six symptom-free
      run-walk sessions.
    - Strengthening: ankle-and-calf 3× per week (continued throughout
      the period).
    - Cycling: easy stationary cycling allowed only when the session
      AND the following day are symptom-free.

2027-01-09 through 2027-01-23 — Strengthening-only blocks
  Seven 7:00–7:20 am Central ankle-and-calf strengthening blocks on
  Sat 01-09, Mon 01-11, Wed 01-13, Sat 01-16, Mon 01-18, Wed 01-20,
  Sat 01-23. These blocks did not authorize running and were kept below
  symptom threshold (controlled calf raises, resisted eversion with a
  band, single-leg balance work near a counter).

================================================================
SECTION B — 20-MINUTE RUN-WALK RESTART (six sessions)
================================================================

Session structure throughout Section B (per 2027-01-08 plan):
  Total session length: 20 minutes.
  Pattern: 4 × (4-minute easy run, 1-minute walk).
  Weekly dose: 2 sessions, non-consecutive days.
  Stop rule: stop immediately for any focal right-ankle pain or any
  gait change.
  Symptom checks: during session, later same day, and following day
  (walking + stairs).

2027-01-26 (Tue) — Run-walk session 1
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min easy run + 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: first authorized restart session after the 14-day gate.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.

RIGHT ANKLE RUNNING REHABILITATION — HISTORICAL CHRONOLOGY
January – April 2027

Prepared for clinician review. This document is a record of what was done
and what was observed during the January–April 2027 rehabilitation period.
It is NOT current clearance, NOT a recommendation to progress, and NOT a
prescription for any future session. All progression decisions remain
subject to direct clinician evaluation.

Working assessment carried into this period (from 2027-01-08 visit):
load-sensitive medial ankle tendon irritation, right side.
Status entering the period: prior two-session 40-minute continuous running
baseline suspended. Running restart gated by 14 consecutive days without
focal pain and a symptom-free 30-minute brisk walk followed by a
symptom-free day. Ankle-and-calf strengthening 3× per week throughout.
Easy stationary cycling only when the session and the following day were
symptom-free.

Note on structure: every session entry below records (1) the session
itself — what was done and at what dose; (2) the spacing relative to the
prior session; (3) the during-session symptom check; (4) the later
same-day symptom check; and (5) the following-day walking and stairs
observation.

================================================================
SECTION A — REHABILITATION FOLLOW-UP AND RESTART GATE
================================================================

2027-01-08 (Fri) — Rehabilitation follow-up visit
  Clinician findings: no swelling, no instability, no gait change, no
  sign of acute bone injury. Assessment unchanged — load-sensitive
  medial ankle tendon irritation, right ankle.
  Plan in effect on exit:
    - Former 40-minute two-session baseline: SUSPENDED.
    - Gating conditions before running may resume: 14 consecutive days
      without focal pain, then a symptom-free 30-minute brisk walk
      followed by a symptom-free day.
    - Restart prescription once gates met: two non-consecutive 20-minute
      sessions per week, alternating four-minute easy runs with
      one-minute walks.
    - Continuous running: requires review after six symptom-free
      run-walk sessions.
    - Strengthening: ankle-and-calf 3× per week (continued throughout
      the period).
    - Cycling: easy stationary cycling allowed only when the session
      AND the following day are symptom-free.

2027-01-09 through 2027-01-23 — Strengthening-only blocks
  Seven 7:00–7:20 am Central ankle-and-calf strengthening blocks on
  Sat 01-09, Mon 01-11, Wed 01-13, Sat 01-16, Mon 01-18, Wed 01-20,
  Sat 01-23. These blocks did not authorize running and were kept below
  symptom threshold (controlled calf raises, resisted eversion with a
  band, single-leg balance work near a counter).

================================================================
SECTION B — 20-MINUTE RUN-WALK RESTART (six sessions)
================================================================

Session structure throughout Section B (per 2027-01-08 plan):
  Total session length: 20 minutes.
  Pattern: 4 × (4-minute easy run, 1-minute walk).
  Weekly dose: 2 sessions, non-consecutive days.
  Stop rule: stop immediately for any focal right-ankle pain or any
  gait change.
  Symptom checks: during session, later same day, and following day
  (walking + stairs).

2027-01-26 (Tue) — Run-walk session 1
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min easy run + 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: first authorized restart session after the 14-day gate.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-01-27 (Wed): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-01-30 (Sat) — Run-walk session 2
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min run / 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: 4 days after session 1 (Tue → Sat), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-01-31 (Sun): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-02-02 (Tue) — Run-walk session 3
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min run / 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: 3 days after session 2 (Sat → Tue), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-02-03 (Wed): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-02-06 (Sat) — Run-walk session 4
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min run / 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: 4 days after session 3 (Tue → Sat), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-02-07 (Sun): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-02-10 (Tue) — Run-walk session 5
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min run / 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: 4 days after session 4 (Sat → Tue), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-02-11 (Wed): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-02-13 (Fri) — Run-walk session 6
  Session: 20-minute sequence (4-min run / 1-min walk × 4).
  Spacing: 3 days after session 5 (Tue → Fri), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-02-14 (Sat): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

  Six non-consecutive 20-minute run-walk sessions completed on Tue,
  Sat, Tue, Sat, Tue, Fri — non-consecutive spacing preserved
  throughout; no third weekly session added.
  Every session, every same-day check, and every following-day
  walking-and-stairs check: symptom-free.
  Strengthening 3× per week continued; cycling remained adjunct-only

================================================================

2027-02-19 (Fri) — Interval-progression clinical review
  Evidence presented: six symptom-free 20-minute run-walk sessions
  with symptom-free following days.
  Outcome / new plan:
    - Authorized baseline moved to two non-consecutive 25-minute
      sessions per week, alternating nine-minute easy runs with
      one-minute walks.
    - Continuous running: still NOT approved; requires further review
      after six symptom-free sessions at the 25-minute level.
    - 40-minute baseline: remains SUSPENDED.
    - Strengthening: continue 3× per week.
    - Clinical check scheduled: 2027-03-15 (Mon), 7:30–8:00 am Central.

Session structure for Section D (per 2027-02-19 plan):
  Total session length: 25 minutes.
  Pattern: 2 × (9-minute easy run, 1-minute walk) plus a final
    9-minute easy run (i.e., 9/1/9/1/9).
  Weekly dose: 2 sessions, non-consecutive days.
  Stop rule: stop immediately for any focal right-ankle pain or any
  gait change.
  Symptom checks: during session, later same day, and following day
  (walking + stairs).

================================================================
