================================================================

2027-02-21 (Sun) — 25-min run-walk session 1
  Spacing: 2 days after the 02-19 review; first session at the new
    25-minute tier.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-02-22 (Mon): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-02-24 (Wed) — 25-min run-walk session 2
  Spacing: 3 days after session 1 (Sun → Wed), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-02-25 (Thu): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-02-28 (Sun) — 25-min run-walk session 3
  Spacing: 4 days after session 2 (Wed → Sun), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-03-01 (Mon): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-03-03 (Wed) — 25-min run-walk session 4
  Spacing: 3 days after session 3 (Sun → Wed), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-03-04 (Thu): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-03-07 (Sat) — 25-min run-walk session 5
  Spacing: 4 days after session 4 (Wed → Sat), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-03-08 (Sun): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-03-10 (Tue) — 25-min run-walk session 6
  Spacing: 3 days after session 5 (Sat → Tue), non-consecutive.
  During session: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-03-11 (Wed): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

Section D summary:
  Six non-consecutive 25-minute run-walk sessions completed on Sun,
  Wed, Sun, Wed, Sat, Tue — non-consecutive spacing preserved
  throughout; no third weekly session added.
  Every session, every same-day check, and every following-day
  walking-and-stairs check: symptom-free.
  Strengthening 3× per week continued throughout.
  Continuous running remained unapproved pending the 2027-03-15
  clinical check.

================================================================
SECTION E — CLINICAL CHECK (GATE TO CONTINUOUS RUNNING)
================================================================

2027-03-15 (Mon) — Right ankle clinical check, 7:30–8:00 am Central
  Evidence presented: six symptom-free non-consecutive 25-minute
  run-walk sessions, each with a symptom-free following day.
  Outcome of this check (per clinical authorization):
    - Continuous easy running at 30 minutes per session became the
      authorized working baseline, two non-consecutive sessions per
      week.
    - 35- and 40-minute runs, third weekly sessions, and outdoor bike
      commuting remained UNAPPROVED at exit of this visit.
    - Strengthening: continue 3× per week.

================================================================
SECTION F — INITIAL 30-MINUTE CONTINUOUS BLOCK (two sessions,
              in March, prior to the April block below)
================================================================

Session structure in Section F and Section G (per 2027-03-15 plan):
  Continuous easy run, 30 minutes.
  Weekly dose: 2 sessions, non-consecutive days.
  Stop rule: stop immediately for any focal right-ankle pain or any
  gait change.
  Symptom checks: during session, later same day, and following day
  (walking + stairs).

2027-03-17 (Wed) — First 30-min continuous easy run
  Spacing: 2 days after the 03-15 clinical check; first continuous
    run since the 2027-01-08 suspension.
  During run: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-03-18 (Thu): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-03-21 (Sat) — Second 30-min continuous easy run
  Spacing: 4 days after 03-17 (Wed → Sat), non-consecutive.
  During run: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-03-22 (Sun): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

================================================================
SECTION G — APRIL 30-MINUTE CONTINUOUS BLOCK
              (four sessions, March 22 – April 15)
================================================================

2027-04-04 (Sun) — 30-min continuous easy run #1 of the April block
  Spacing: non-consecutive relative to 03-21 (Wed → Sun → Sun;
    consecutive calendar weeks but sessions remain non-consecutive
    by clinical spacing rule).
  During run: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-04-05 (Mon): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-04-07 (Wed) — 30-min continuous easy run #2 of the April block
  Spacing: 2 days after 04-04 (Sun → Wed), non-consecutive.
  During run: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-04-08 (Thu): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-04-11 (Sun) — 30-min continuous easy run #3 of the April block
  Spacing: 3 days after 04-07 (Wed → Sun), non-consecutive.
  During run: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-04-12 (Mon): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free.

2027-04-14 (Fri) — 30-min continuous easy run #4 of the April block
  Spacing: 3 days after 04-11 (Sun → Fri), non-consecutive.
  During run: no focal right-ankle pain, swelling, instability,
    or gait change.
  Later same day: no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change.
  Following day, 2027-04-15 (Sat): ordinary walking and stairs
    symptom-free through the morning check.

Section G summary:
  Four non-consecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs between
  2027-03-22 and 2027-04-15, on Sun 04-04, Wed 04-07, Sun 04-11,
  and Fri 04-14.
  Every session, every same-day check, and every following-day
  walking-and-stairs check: symptom-free.
  No 35- or 40-minute run attempted; no third weekly session added.
  Strengthening 3× per week continued throughout.
  Outdoor-bike commuting question: not authorized during this
  window; remained open and pending clinician direction at the
  close of the period.

================================================================
SECTION H — CONSISTENT BACKGROUND PRACTICES (Jan–Apr 2027)
================================================================

  - Ankle-and-calf strengthening: 3× per week throughout, kept below
    symptom threshold.
  - Stationary cycling: allowed only when both the session and the
    following day were symptom-free; not used as a substitute for the
    run-walk evidence requirement.
  - Stop rule applied at every session: immediate stop on any focal
    right-ankle pain or any gait change. The rule was not triggered
    during the January–April 2027 period.
  - Baseline suspensions and approvals were tracked against the
    clinician's gating conditions, not self-escalated.

================================================================
SECTION I — DOCUMENT STATUS NOTE
================================================================

  This document is HISTORY. It records the rehabilitation sessions
  that were completed and the symptom observations that accompanied
  them between 2027-01-08 and 2027-04-15.

  This document is NOT current clearance to run at any specific
  duration, frequency, or intensity.

  This document is NOT a recommendation for any future progression,
  including any extension past 30 minutes, any third weekly session,
  any outdoor bike commuting, or any other change to the running or
  loading baseline.

  Any progression decision — including continuation, modification,
  or pause — requires direct clinician evaluation and authorization.

tests.request: Create a compact hypothesis-number crosswalk document for the archived Feb–Apr 2023 mid-segment churn investigation, preserving the original H1–H4 ordering so readers can decode later numbered references correctly.

input.body:
Purpose
-------
Compact decoder so any later numbered reference (e.g. "see H3" in the institutional doc, the Apr 10 lift writeup, the May 12 all-hands deck, or the cohort-cut appendix) maps back to the correct hypothesis in its original H1–H4 slot. Original ordering is preserved; do not renumber.

Original hypothesis stack (Feb 7, 2023 skeleton — order locked)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- H1 — Pricing artifact
- H2 — Competitor cycle / generic seasonal
- H3 — Onboarding timing (lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2)
- H4 — CS coverage

Crosswalk
---------
- H1  Pricing artifact
     Original claim: the Feb 5.1% mid-seg spike is driven by a pricing-page change.
     Tier-cut (entry / standard / plus), first pass 2023-02-13, deadline 2023-02-15.
     Verdict (2023-02-15, posted to #growth-investigations tagging Priya, Marcus Vail, Tomas): DEAD — does not hold when cut by tier.
     Adjacent caveat: Marcus's pricing-page rev experiment never got a clean read because the 3/2 signup-form layout change was concurrent; H1 verdict stands separately from that test.
     See also: parked H1 attribution note in the investigation doc (docc_1789203715216 thread).

- H2  Competitor cycle / generic seasonal
     Original claim: the Feb spike is a recurring February / market-event pattern.
     Cut (2023-02-17 → locked 2023-02-21): historical Feb 2021 and Feb 2022 churn rates were 2.0–2.2% with no matching spike.
     Verdict (2023-02-21): DEAD — competitor-cycle and generic seasonal explanations rejected.
     Locked-rhythm prerequisite order: (1) spike-start timestamp + candidate competitor event list, (2) Feb priors + adjacent months, (3) Owen cohort logic via Jan-scan template, (4) execute cut, (5) Owen 1-pager (why / cuts / p-value / effect / call).

- H3  Onboarding timing (lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2)
     Original claim: the day-7 onboarding email is firing at the wrong moment for mid-seg.
     Scope per doc-comment update: mid-segment only; registry flag at 50% rollout; n = 400; 2-week window; scope-disjoint from the pricing-page test.
     Activation-day re-run (same Jan-scan + Owen cohort logic, n = 210): pre-onboarding-hit bucket 3.1% churn vs. post-day-7 / pre-activation bucket 7.8% churn → 4.7-point gap, first load-bearing signal in the investigation.
     First-cut checkpoints 2/24 and 2/28 remain parked, not being called.
     Operational lock (the rule we shipped with): the Apr 10 onboarding-trigger v2 lift is the actual signal; the Apr 17–20 wobble was a one-week scare from 50–75 seat contamination, not a regression (city-planner book-club framing); 50–75 is now the starter cohort, so the Feb spike recomputed under the old (50–200) definition gives the wrong number.

- H4  CS coverage
     Original claim: CS coverage on mid-seg is thin and predicts weirdness in the smaller mid-seg accounts.
     Status: expected to drop if H3 confirms (deadline posture set 2023-02-09). Remained open through the institutional-doc draft (2023-05-08) and is the standing "watch item" alongside the parked lifecycle-email gating question behind H3.

Decoder notes for later numbered references
-------------------------------------------
- "H3 first-cut" / "2/24 or 2/28 cut" → the parked H3 activation-timing reads, not a called result.
- "5.1 → 3.8% recovery" → refers to the mid-seg monthly churn trajectory; the recovery is real even after the bucket moved because Owen v2-backfilled the historicals under mid_seg v2 (50–200 reads retained under mid_seg v1 for comparison). Locked point (1) in the institutional doc.
- "Apr 10 lift" → H3 onboarding-trigger v2 signal; the rule we ship with.
- "Apr 17–20 wobble" → 50–75 contamination scare inside H3, not a regression.
- "50–75 removed from mid-segment" / "50–75 is the starter cohort" → cohort-definition change that closes H3 cleanly and invalidates any old-definition recompute of the Feb spike.
- "City-planner book club" frame → the explanation device used 2023-05-03 to defend the Apr 10 lift against the Apr 17–20 wobble and to justify the 50–75 removal.

Boundaries preserved in doc comments
------------------------------------
- H1 ↔ Marcus's pricing-page rev experiment: kept separate; do not collapse.
- H3 ↔ pricing-page signup-form layout change (3/2): confound flagged to Daniela; onboarding experiment not advanced to running and rollout not increased until engineering sign-off.
- H4 ↔ lifecycle-email gating: parked behind H3; stays on the radar while the investigation is closed.

Reference docs
--------------
- Living investigation doc: "Mid-seg churn spike -- Feb 2023 investigation" (opened 2023-02-07, doc-comment ID docc_1789203715216).
- Institutional writeup: "Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 -- what we learned" (started 2023-04-29, final draft 2023-05-08, sent to Priya and Tomas for review; six pages + one-page exec summary + cohort-cut appendix).
- All-hands delivery: 2023-05-12, ~140 attendees, 15-min talk + 10-min Q&A, method-forward framing.

tests.request: Create a Helio Start change-sequencing checklist. For packaging, a pricing-page experiment, paid acquisition, and activation measurement, state what must be settled first. Present each prerequisite with the downstream work it blocks, and preserve any required separation between measurement populations.
tests.answer:
HELIO START — CHANGE-SEQUENCING CHECKLIST (2028-01-01)

Purpose: for each downstream change (packaging, pricing-page experiment, paid acquisition, activation measurement), state what must be settled first, what work that prerequisite blocks, and the measurement-population separations to preserve.

The order below restates the accepted decision (eligibility/refusal before packaging, taxonomy/entitlements before the pricing-page experiment, lifecycle fork before paid acquisition, activation measurement separate from retained mid-segment). It does not promote any item into scope.

NON-GOALS (do not promote into scope during this sequence):
  [ ] Pricing-page exposure / GA promotion
  [ ] Paid acquisition
  [ ] Launch or pipeline framing
  [ ] Q4 revenue credit for Helio Start
  [ ] Concurrent activation/retention + lifecycle + feature-flag experiments

DOWNSTREAM ITEM 1 — PACKAGING

  Must be settled first:
    [ ] Eligibility rules (admin proof, simple deployment, connector access,
        external authority, current entitlement, supported billing) —
        certifiable inputs in hand
    [ ] Refusal rules (unresolved ownership, imports, migrations, manual
        billing, agencies) — Priya sign-off

  What this prerequisite blocks until cleared:
    - Pricing-page copy decisions (headline, subhead, body, CTA)
    - Lifecycle entry-touch design
    - Paid-acquisition creative
    - Pipeline attribution
    - Any claim that HS admission is automatic or instant

  Reason it must go first:
    Packaging copy mirrors the live admission boundary. Until refusal
    rules are signed off, packaging either over-promises (creating
    ineligible intake) or under-promises (suppressing eligible intake).
    Both corrupt measurement. The refusal list is the gate.

DOWNSTREAM ITEM 2 — PRICING-PAGE EXPERIMENT

  Must be settled first:
    [ ] Event taxonomy (helio-start-event-taxonomy-spec) QA-clean
    [ ] Entitlements instrumentation — source-of-truth field for initial
        entitlement, update events for support handoff and billing
        exceptions, no-plan-name-inference rule, backfill policy
        documented
    [ ] Billing sign-off on the entitlement path
    [ ] Confirmation that the entitlement instrumentation no longer
        blocks the late-July readiness review

  What this prerequisite blocks until cleared:
    - Any headline or subhead variation
    - Reordering of the comparison cards
    - Mobile accordion collapse of the feature table
    - Any pricing-page change other than the already-approved HS entry
      and eligibility path
    - Attribution reads between pricing-page changes and HS activation

  Reason it must go first:
    A pricing-page experiment needs a defensible measure of
    "eligibility-flow starts" and of the workspace's entitlement state.
    Without QA-clean taxonomy and entitlement instrumentation, no clean
    attribution can be drawn and the experiment contaminates the HS
    activation report.

  Concurrency rule (standing preference):
    Do not run this experiment concurrently with activation/retention,
    lifecycle, or feature-flag experiments. Keep the experimental
    surface quiet during growth-stage reviews.

DOWNSTREAM ITEM 3 — PAID ACQUISITION

  Must be settled first:
    [ ] Lifecycle fork boundaries — education-only touches confirmed;
        state-changing branches remain blocked until entitlement state,
        admin complexity, and support handoff signals are live
    [ ] Routing confirmed for refused and out-of-scope applicants
    [ ] Connector-access change live in the HS intake

  What this prerequisite blocks until cleared:
    - Any paid search batch (including the conditionally approved batch
      currently held for offline review before 2027-11-01)
    - Any directory or referral listing carrying utm attribution
    - Any retargeting or audience list tied to HS
    - Any HS pipeline forecast or revenue credit
    - Any reallocation of underspend (for example the $6,237.50 Q1
      reserve) into HS paid — underspend is not reallocation authority
      and it inverts the agreed sequence

  Reason it must go first:
    Paid acquisition is the highest-stakes lever. Shipping it before
    the lifecycle fork inverts the sequence, creates attribution that
    contaminates the organic pricing-page channel, and turns a reserve
    into a launch signal.

  Customer-facing copy constraints (carry into any future paid
  creative — phrases below conflict with the live admission and
  assisted-routing boundaries and must not appear):
    - "for every team"
    - "launch in minutes"
    - "skip assisted handoffs"
    - "start setup immediately"
    - "every team under 50 seats can create a workspace in minutes"
    - "no review required"
    - "new self-serve plan from the pricing page"

DOWNSTREAM ITEM 4 — ACTIVATION MEASUREMENT

  Must be settled first:
    [ ] No additional sequencing prerequisite from this list —
        measurement runs on its own track.
    [ ] Confirmation that the live view (Owen) keeps HS reporting
        structurally separate from ordinary starter activation,
        retained mid-segment v2 (75–200), Expansion Assist, and the
        50–75 band view.

  What this prerequisite blocks / preserves:
    - Any merge of HS activation into ordinary starter activation
    - Any merge of HS support load into retained mid-segment support
      load
    - Any merge of HS funnel into Expansion Assist reporting
    - Any HS line in paid-acquisition target, pipeline goal, or
      forecast
    - Counting the imported sandbox first-integration event in HS
      post-admission activation — it stays in audit history only

  Required measurement populations (do not collapse):
    - HS eligible starts: workspaces that pass the public eligibility
      check
    - HS activation rate: workspaces with a first integration within
      seven days ÷ activated workspaces
    - HS support load: (ordinary setup questions + permissions or
      ownership reviews) ÷ activated workspaces, reported per 100
    - HS routed-before-setup: a separate count, not folded into
      support load
    - HS segment view: HS on its own line; retained mid-segment and
      Expansion Assist on their own lines

  Reason the separation is structural, not a filter:
    HS carries its own admission, lifecycle, and segment-economics
    boundaries. Saying it is structural (not a filter) preempts readers
    from inferring that ordinary starter or retained mid-segment share
    HS's invite-cohort operating path.

CROSS-ITEM SEPARATION CHECKLIST (do not let these merge):
  [ ] HS admission boundary ≠ ordinary starter admission boundary
  [ ] HS support load ≠ retained mid-segment support load
  [ ] HS lifecycle fork ≠ expansion nudge (EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge)
  [ ] HS activation rate ≠ Expansion Assist activation rate
  [ ] HS pipeline forecast ≠ Q4 revenue credit
  [ ] HS imported-sandbox first-integration event ≠ HS post-admission
      activation

ITEMS REMAINING OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS SEQUENCE:
  [ ] Pricing-page exposure / GA
  [ ] Paid acquisition
  [ ] Pipeline attribution / launch framing
  [ ] Q4 revenue credit for HS
  [ ] Concurrent experimental surface (activation/retention + lifecycle
      + feature-flag)

The checklist is a restatement, not a scope expansion. If you want it saved as a doc, I can create it in the Growth folder alongside the existing Helio Start working documents — say the word and I will.

tests.request: Historical analyses may still reference activation definition v2. Create a warehouse glossary note documenting its exact criteria, the period when it was the active cut, and what should happen to that definition after its replacement.

input.body:
Status (as of 2028-01-01): Retired. v3 ("first integration + at least one in-product event within 14 days") is the active cut. v1 ("first integration in 14 days", established Aug 2022, unchanged) remains available for back-compat. Historical analyses from the v2 era may still reference v2 — those references are frozen, not live.

Exact criteria. A workspace is activated under v2 iff BOTH of the following are true within 14 days of signup:
  1. The workspace records a first_integration event (any connector completes first sync), AND
  2. The workspace records at least two distinct login sessions tied to that workspace within the same 14-day window.
The two-login requirement is what made v2 "UI-shaped" — accounts that integrated once and then lived in API, CLI, or embedded use were systematically excluded. This is the documented reason Riley flagged v2 for replacement.

input.body:
# Wallet Reference — Current Travel Card

Card product in effect since June 15, 2027 (product change completed before the April 14, 2025 fee deadline).

## Annual fee
- $0

## Earning rates
- Travel and dining: 1.5 rewards points per $1
- Everything else: 1 point per $1

## Points — what happened to existing and pending balances
- Existing points: remain in the same rewards account. Nothing was forfeited, converted, or transferred.
- Pending points: also remain in the same rewards account. They will post there as usual.
- Account opening date and credit line were preserved by the product change, so point history and credit profile are unchanged.

## Travel benefits to NO LONGER count on when booking
- $75 annual travel credit — ended immediately when the card was changed. Do not budget for it on any trip.
- Lounge passes — ended immediately when the card was changed. No lounge access through this card; assume none until proven otherwise.
- Any airline incidental credits, baggage fee waivers, or other premium-card travel perks tied to the old product are gone.

## Still useful for booking
- 1.5x earn on travel and dining (per the issuer's category definitions for flights, hotels, cruises, car rentals, restaurants, etc.).
- Points continue to accrue to the same rewards account; redeem through the standard rewards portal.

## Quick sanity check before you book
- No annual fee to recoup.
- No $75 credit to chase.
- No lounge access to plan around.
- Net annual cost: $0.

tests.request: Create a document containing a one-metric card for our historical rollout evidence covering the third post-ship onboarding cohort; include the cohort context, metric, comparison basis, and measured change, and keep it strictly descriptive without causal or forecasting claims.

input.body:
# One-Metric Card — Third Post-Ship Onboarding Cohort

## Cohort Context
- Onboarding cohort: third post-ship cohort (2024-04-22 start), after the onboarding-trigger v2 100% rollout on 2024-04-10.
- Eligible population: 61 admitted workspaces in the cohort window.
- Activation definition held constant: v3 guardrail (first_integration + ≥1 in-product event within 14 days).
- Observation window: 14-day v3 window.

## Metric
- Activation rate: 48 activated of 61 eligible workspaces = 78.7%.

## Comparison Basis
- Prior cohorts in the post-ship sequence, same v3 activation definition:
  - Cohort 1 (2024-04-04): 23 of 34 = 67.6%.
  - Cohort 2 (2024-04-09): 44 of 58 = 75.9%.
  - Cohort 3 (2024-04-22): 48 of 61 = 78.7%.
- Combined across the three post-ship cohorts: 115 of 153 = 75.2%.
- Cross-check against the mix-standardized read on the broader rollout pair: ~58.9% standardized activation estimate versus a prior cohort 57.2%, a ~1.7-point descriptive difference on top of a +4.6-point crude move.

## Measured Change
- Cohort 3 vs Cohort 2: +2.8 percentage points (75.9% → 78.7%) on the same v3 definition.
- Cohort 3 vs Cohort 1: +11.1 percentage points (67.6% → 78.7%) on the same v3 definition.
- Across the three-cohort post-ship sequence, the within-window activation rate moved from 67.6% to 78.7%, an aggregate +11.1 percentage points over the two intervening cohorts.

## Notes
- This card reports what was measured against the defined comparison basis only.
- No causal claim is made and no ship claim is made.
- No forecast of future cohorts is made.

tests.request: Create a short historical framing note for the completed February-April 2023 mid-segment churn investigation.
tests.answer:
Here is the historical framing note.

---
Historical Framing Note — Mid-Segment Churn Investigation, Feb–Apr 2023
Author: Riley Tanaka
Date: 2028-01-01
Purpose: Retrospective frame for the institutional record; references the artifact set produced and the lessons that later informed funnel/lifecycle work.

In February 2023, mid-segment monthly churn printed 5.1% on the then-operating cohort cut (50–200 paid seats), a sharp break from historical Feb baselines of 2.0%–2.2% in 2021 and 2022 and from any matching movement in adjacent segments. A live investigation doc was opened 2023-02-07 to hold baselines, hypothesis list, and cohort cuts as each analysis pass landed.

Two initially plausible explanations were ruled out early using the same cohort logic as the January scan: a competitor-pricing-cycle narrative and a generic seasonal Q1 dip. The historical Feb readings showed neither pattern, so the spike was treated as a real product/segment signal rather than a market artifact.

The end-of-April snapshot closed the case. Mid-segment churn stabilized at 3.8% on the v2 cut (75–200 paid seats), down from the 5.1% Feb 7 reading on the old bucket. Two drivers were identified: an April 10 onboarding-trigger v2 lift that held despite an April 17–20 wobble, and a mid-segment scope change that removed 50–75-seat accounts, which had been inflating the raw rate. Owen backfilled the historicals on the v2 relabel so the recovery was not an artifact of the definition change alone.

The investigation was finalized 2023-05-08 as a 6-page write-up plus a 1-page executive summary and a cohort-cut appendix, reviewed by Priya and Tomas. A scope-disjoint footnote (docc_1789203715216) documented the v2 operating cut for downstream readers.

Lessons that later informed funnel/lifecycle work:
  - Cohort-cut discipline: hold the operating cut stable, or backfill before comparison.
  - Spikes need historical baselines before any hypothesis gets narrative weight.
  - Definition changes can mimic recoveries; relabel backfill is the antidote.

Archival. The original investigation doc and supporting cohort cuts remain the authoritative reference.

---

Two things to flag:

1. I have not verified the original Notion doc ID for "Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 -- what we learned" — I noted docc_1789203715216 is on the earlier "Mid-seg churn spike -- Feb 2023 investigation" doc, not the finalized write-up. tests.request: Create a short document titled `April 2023 onboarding and mid-segment analysis — data-quality erratum` so future readers do not reuse the stale cohort logic; include the corrected cohort boundary and both the classification and timing issues that made the original read noisier.

input.body:
Scope
- Erratum for the April 2023 onboarding-trigger and mid-segment reads (cohort midseg_75_200_v2 and predecessor definitions). Two independent data-quality issues made the original v2 readout noisier than the underlying signal. This note records the corrected cohort boundary and the two issues so future readers do not reuse the stale logic.

Corrected cohort boundary
- Use: mid-segment = 75–200 seats (cohort key: midseg_75_200_v2).
- Do NOT use the prior 50–200-seat mid-segment definition. The 50–75-seat band belongs to SMB and is excluded from mid.

Issue 1 — classification (segment job)
- The segment job misclassified a chunk of 50–75-seat accounts as mid-segment.
- Effect: those accounts inflated the mid-segment denominator. They are not a real mid-segment population and should never have entered the cohort.
- Resolution: rebuild the cohort at 75–200 seats; the 50–75 misclassified rows are dropped.

Issue 2 — timing (onboarding send, cache window)
- The onboarding send read stale membership off the cache window, so it applied the new trigger logic to accounts whose seat count had already moved out of the cohort since the last cache refresh.
- Effect: the denominator was wrong before retention was even measured. Retention on the mis-tagged rows looked like v2 noise; it was actually a tagging artifact.
- Resolution: re-derive the cohort from a fresh membership snapshot taken at trigger time, not from the cached read.

Why this matters going forward
- Any read that mixes the old 50–200 boundary with the new trigger logic will attribute classification noise and cache-window noise to the trigger. Do not splice pre-Apr-10 boundary cases into the post-correction cohort without re-tagging.
- The Apr 10 onboarding-trigger v2 lift is real on the corrected 75–200 cohort. The Apr 17–20 wobble is explained by the CS auto-nudge outage, not by the trigger.
- Spot-check rule: before trusting any comparison line that crosses the Apr 10 boundary, manually inspect one pre-cut cohort under the corrected tagging logic.

Reference
- Companion doc: "Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 -- what we learned" (kept as the living analysis pass log).

tests.request: Create an archive note dated April 17, 2023, explaining the temporary second-post-ship cohort dip, the outage duration, and the system's condition after the incident. Do not include an exact outage start or end date.

input.body:
Archive Note — April 17, 2023
Subject: Second post-ship cohort retention dip (root cause: CS-side outage)

Summary
On April 17, 2023, the second post-ship cohort posted a week-1 retention read of +1.4 pts versus baseline, materially below the April 10 cohort (+3.2 pts) and the pooled experiment read (+3.1 pts). The dip is temporary and fully explained by an upstream CS-side incident, not by a regression in the lifecycle or onboarding systems themselves.

Outage Duration
A CS-side outage affecting the auto-onboarding-nudge system lasted roughly 36 hours in mid-April. The exact start and end timestamps are still owed by Daniela and will be appended to this note when received. No exact outage start or end date is recorded here by design, pending the official timeline from the CS reliability owner.

Root Cause
During the outage window, two upstream systems were out of spec:

- CS auto-onboarding-nudge: down for the duration of the incident; nudge sends did not fire.
- Segment / membership-freshness: the segment job misclassified a chunk of 50–75-seat accounts as mid, and the onboarding send read stale membership off the cache window. This distorted the denominator before retention was measured, which made `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` look noisier than it actually was.

The nudge outage shifted activation timing for the affected cohort, producing the April 17 artifact at the cohort cut. Signup source and tier cuts remained clean throughout — Marcus confirmed this on the April 21 board call. `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` operated as designed: it fired later relative to signup but did not align with the cohort cut, which is what created the apparent dip rather than any failure inside the trigger itself.

System Condition After the Incident
- CS auto-onboarding-nudge: restored; currently back up and firing normally.
- Segment / membership-freshness: stale-membership cache window has cleared; segment job classification for 50–75-seat accounts is back to spec.
- `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`: no failure; behavior consistent with design, just observed against a shifted activation baseline.

Disposition
- Owen will exclude the April 17 data point from any lift average.
- Cohort 3 readout is expected the week of April 24–28, 2023, and will serve as the clean confirmation read.
- Footnote for the doc: "Wobble = cohort 2 dip attributed to the CS-side outage (signup source + tier cuts clean)."
- Daniela's outage timestamps and zero-send telemetry remain the open item to close the April 17 paperwork.

This note is archival. It is not a clearance for the 45-minute activation bump and does not change the standing evidence-only posture on cohort reads until the cohort 3 confirmation lands.

tests.request: Please create a brief historical decision-rights note titled “July 2023 decision rights — Helio Start and retained-mid expansion” for our governance retrospective. Cover both workstreams during July 2023, distinguish the strategic decision lane from routine execution, and explicitly label the note as a period-specific record rather than current org policy.

input.body:
Historical decision-rights note — July 2023

Status: Period-specific record. Captures who held which decision lanes during July 2023 across the Helio Start and retained-mid Expansion Assist workstreams. Not current organizational policy; lane boundaries and naming have evolved since.

Workstreams in scope
1. Helio Start — guarded pre-discovery product through July; August beta gated on eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, and support clearance.
2. Expansion Assist, retained-mid segment — behavior-gated expansion-nudge exploration; not framed as a Helio Start proof point or a Q3 forecast item.

Strategic decision lane (kept by Riley)
- Gate arbitration across the four Helio Start August-beta preconditions.
- Refusal-list finalization and the rule that governs what does not get rolled forward.
- Entitlement sequencing checks with Daniela.
- Cross-functional tradeoffs where decision rules, scope, or language cross workstreams.
- Forecast, board, causal-claim, and executive-language decisions, including the rule against forecastable Q3 revenue language on these workstreams.
- Helio Start reporting scope decision: bounded-GA public product reported inside the existing four-consumer reporting scope, separate from retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls.

Routine execution lane
- Owen — readout shapes. Owns the first-pass Helio Start baseline readout (pre-discovery) and the behavior-gated retained-mid Expansion Assist eligibility cuts (high-depth n=118 exploratory, criteria tightened post-spec). Source-completeness closure sits with Owen.
- Ines — lifecycle fork risk map and copy-boundary work. Covers Helio Start copy boundaries (no pricing-page copy, no launch-timing language) and the expansion-nudge learning (in-product plus channel, both explicit). Lane is bounded to routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews; does not extend to other consumers.
- Daniela — engineering, release, and rollback controls, including entitlement sequencing inputs.

How the lanes were used in July
- The July operating update kept owner lanes informal, reusing the existing investigation framework rather than running a formal Helio process.
- Helio Start stayed guarded pre-discovery through the month; no August beta was opened because none of the four gates had cleared.
- The expansion nudge did not meet the blanket-rollout bar; it informed a behavior-based Expansion Assist follow-on, kept separate from Helio Start reporting.
- The naming convention adopted for lifecycle segments used an `hs_` prefix for Helio Start and an `ea_` prefix for retained-mid Expansion Assist (example: `active_admin_ready` → `hs_setup_fit`), reflecting the scope-separation rule above.

End of period-specific record.

input.body:
STATUS: EXPIRED HISTORICAL REFERENCE — 2024 Holiday Season Only
This card documents a private-event policy that applied during the 2024 holiday season. It is retained for archival purposes and is NOT current operating policy. Do not use for active bookings.

Scope
- Roasted chicken is an advance-count private-event option only.
- It is NOT a weekly menu item and was NOT promoted or served as one.
- Production method: Sam's tested pre-staging sequence (unchanged).

Booking limits (one-case booking)
- Maximum commitment: 23 guest chicken portions.
- Protected contingency: 2 kitchen-only portions (reserved, not advertised, not offered as seconds; default to staff meal).
- Ordering beyond 23 guest portions exceeds the policy cap.

Deadlines
- Final entree split (chicken vs. vegetarian): due 7 days before service (firm-count deadline).

Relationship to the weekly menu
- Separate from the weekly menu; no recurring standing commitment.
- Standardization flowed one-way; Sam's restaurant role unaffected.

Reminder
- This is expired historical reference material. For any current private-event inquiry, consult current policy, not this card.

input.body:
PATIENT: Riley Tanaka
DATE OF VISIT: 2027-11-05
CLINICIAN: Physical therapy — right ankle reassessment
RECORD AUTHOR: Patient (self-prepared, for clinician review)

==================================================
1. REASON FOR VISIT
==================================================
Routine reassessment of the stable right-ankle running baseline prior to any consideration of progression. Background: recurrent focal medial right-ankle tendon irritation; most recent rehabilitation course completed in early 2027 after a focal-ache recurrence. Continuous running was resumed on a 40-minute easy lake-trail baseline (established 2026-01-19) under established progression rules. Patient requested this visit to review the six-run tolerance evidence at the 40-minute level and to confirm continued authorization before the next winter block.

==================================================
2. SUBJECTIVE REPORT AT 2027-11-05
==================================================
At the time of the visit, the patient reported:
- No recurrence of focal inside-right-ankle pain at rest.
- No gait change.
- No swelling.
- No instability.
- Maintenance of the authorized baseline: two nonconsecutive 40-minute easy morning lake-trail sessions per week, kept off Tuesday and Thursday commute days.
- Tuesday and Thursday: bike commute only, each leg ≤25 minutes at easy effort. No run on a commute day.
- Continued ankle-and-calf strengthening three times per week.
- Symptom-check rule honored after every run (during session, remainder of day, and following morning of ordinary walking and stairs).

==================================================
3. CLINICAL FINDINGS (per patient report of visit)
==================================================
- No focal ankle tenderness on examination.
- No swelling.
- No instability.
- No altered gait.
- No sign of acute bone injury.

==================================================
4. CLINICIAN DETERMINATION
==================================================
- Therapist did NOT authorize progression beyond the current 40-minute baseline.
- Patient continues the current authorized plan as written in Section 5.
- Any future progression (e.g., 45-minute bump, third weekly session, additional bike day, return of intervals or hills) requires a separate clinical review with the six-session symptom-free evidence and an explicit new authorization.

==================================================
5. AUTHORIZED RUNNING PLAN (effective 2027-11-05)
==================================================
Running baseline:
- Two nonconsecutive 40-minute continuous easy runs per week on the morning lake trail.
- Effort: easy / conversational.
- Days: off Tuesday and Thursday (commute days). No run on a bike-commute day.
- Footwear: standard replacement neutral shoes (8 mm drop, 9.2 oz geometry), unchanged from baseline.

Adjunct activity:
- Easy stationary cycling is an adjunct, NOT a progression track.
- Bike-commute legs on Tuesday and Thursday: ≤25 minutes per leg, easy effort.
- No additional bike days beyond Tuesday and Thursday.

Strengthening:
- Ankle-and-calf strengthening three times per week (20-minute morning block).
- Continues regardless of run schedule.

Standing rules (unchanged):
- Symptom check is required after every session: during the run, during the remainder of the day, and during the following morning of ordinary walking and stairs.
- Stop conditions: any focal inside-right-ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change.
  - Focal pain or gait change during a run or the following day ends the progression; sessions revert to 30 minutes and the patient contacts the clinic if focal pain recurs.
  - Recurrent focal pain requires clinical follow-up before further running.
- No self-directed hop testing.
- No 45-minute runs, no third weekly run, no additional bike day, no hills, no intervals — until a future clinical review explicitly authorizes them.

==================================================
6. EVIDENCE ON RECORD (40-MINUTE TOLERANCE BLOCK)
==================================================
Authorized plan from prior clinical review required six symptom-free 40-minute sessions, each followed by a symptom-free next day, before a reassessment visit. Logged sessions to date:

  Initial six sessions:
  - 2027-11-07 (Sun) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-11-08 follow-up symptom-free. Run off commute day. Strengthening x3 that week. No third run, no extra bike.
  - 2027-11-10 (Wed) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-11-11 follow-up symptom-free. Run off commute day. No third run, no extra bike.
  - 2027-11-14 (Sun) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-11-15 follow-up symptom-free. Run off commute day. Strengthening x3 that week. No third run, no extra bike.
  - 2027-11-17 (Wed) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-11-18 follow-up symptom-free. Run off commute day. No third run, no extra bike.
  - 2027-11-21 (Sun) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-11-22 follow-up symptom-free. Run off commute day. No third run, no extra bike.
  - 2027-11-24 (Wed) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-11-25 follow-up symptom-free. Run off commute day. No third run, no extra bike.

  Additional sessions logged before the 2027-11-05 visit (kept on non-commute days, both +following day symptom-free):
  - 2027-12-04 (Sat) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-12-05 follow-up symptom-free. No third run, no extra bike.
  - 2027-12-08 (Wed) — 40 min easy lake trail; run, same-day, and 2027-12-09 follow-up symptom-free. No third run, no extra bike.

Through the date of this record, total symptom-free 40-minute runs logged: eight. No third weekly run attempted. No additional bike day added. Strengthening maintained at three sessions per week.

==================================================
7. ITEMS NOT AUTHORIZED AT THIS VISIT
==================================================
- 45-minute runs — not authorized; any bump in session length requires a separate clinical review.
- Third weekly running session — not authorized.
- Additional bike day beyond Tuesday/Thursday commute legs — not authorized.
- Hills, intervals, tempo work, or any intensity progression — not authorized.
- Race or event-specific training — not authorized.
- Return of formal hop testing as a self-screen — not authorized.

==================================================
8. NEXT CLINICAL TOUCHPOINT
==================================================
- Next clinical check is NOT pre-scheduled. The patient will request a visit when (a) seeking authorization for any progression item in Section 7, or (b) experiencing recurrent focal pain, swelling, instability, or gait change per the stop conditions.
- Between visits, the patient maintains this record's Sections 5 and 6 as the active plan.

==================================================
9. PATIENT ATTESTATION
==================================================
The patient prepared this record from session logs and prior clinical notes for clinician review. The patient confirms that the information above accurately reflects the activity performed and the symptoms (or absence of symptoms) experienced, and that no run, bike day, or strengthening session has been added beyond what is described.

— End of record —

tests.request: Create a document containing the historical decision rule for how evidence about onboarding timing would affect the priority of the Customer Success coverage hypothesis.

input.body:
DECISION RULE (as set during the churn investigation, Feb 2023)

Premise
- H1 (pricing artifact) and H2 (competitor cycle) are closed.
- H3 (onboarding timing — day-7 email / activation-state gating) remains open.
- H4 (Customer Success coverage gap) has not yet landed.

Conditional priority for H4 (CS coverage cut)
- If H3 confirms (onboarding timing is a real driver of churn, with effect visible after baseline work settles — target sharpening ~Feb 28), THEN H4 priority is expected to DROP.
- Rationale: a confirmed onboarding-timing cause weakens the case that a CS-coverage cut is the binding constraint, because the bulk of the preventable churn would be addressed by fixing onboarding rather than expanding CS coverage.
- Conversely, if H3 does NOT confirm (onboarding timing is ruled out or materially weakens), H4 remains — or rises — as the active candidate, and the CS-coverage investigation is promoted rather than deprioritized.

Sequencing guardrails captured at the time
- H1 must be decided (dead or alive) by Feb 15, and must stay analytically separate from Marcus's pricing-page test (no smearing of pricing-page experiment effects into the H1 read).
- H2 competitor-cycle rule-out window: Feb 18–21.
- H3 read expected to sharpen ~Feb 28 after baseline work settles; do not promote H4 before that point.
- Both the onboarding-trigger experiment and the pricing-page test target mid-segment week-1 retention, so any layout change (e.g., the 3/2 layout change) that shifts cohort timing must be accounted for in the H3 read before drawing the H3 → H4 conclusion.

Operational form of the rule
- Default: hold H4 in a "watch / not-promoted" state while H3 is open.
- Trigger A (H3 confirms): re-rank H4 downward; redirect CS-coverage investigation effort to onboarding remediation design.
- Trigger B (H3 weakens / fails to confirm): re-rank H4 upward; stand up the CS-coverage investigation as the next active hypothesis.

This rule was in force heading into the late-Feb 2023 re-ranking window and is recorded here as the historical decision rule for how onboarding-timing evidence was intended to move CS-coverage priority.

- Rationale: a confirmed onboarding-timing cause weakens the case that a CS-coverage cut is the binding constraint, because the bulk of the preventable churn would be addressed by fixing onboarding rather than expanding CS coverage.
- Conversely, if H3 does NOT confirm (onboarding timing is ruled out or materially weakens), H4 remains — or rises — as the active candidate, and the CS-coverage investigation is promoted rather than deprioritized.

Sequencing guardrails captured at the time
- H1 must be decided (dead or alive) by Feb 15, and must stay analytically separate from Marcus's pricing-page test (no smearing of pricing-page experiment effects into the H1 read).
- H2 competitor-cycle rule-out window: Feb 18–21.
- H3 read expected to sharpen ~Feb 28 after baseline work settles; do not promote H4 before that point.
- Both the onboarding-trigger experiment and the pricing-page test target mid-segment week-1 retention, so any layout change (e.g., the 3/2 layout change) that shifts cohort timing must be accounted for in the H3 read before drawing the H3 → H4 conclusion.

Operational form of the rule
- Default: hold H4 in a "watch / not-promoted" state while H3 is open.
- Trigger A (H3 confirms): re-rank H4 downward; redirect CS-coverage investigation effort to onboarding remediation design.
- Trigger B (H3 weakens / fails to confirm): re-rank H4 upward; stand up the CS-coverage investigation as the next active hypothesis.

This rule was in force heading into the late-Feb 2023 re-ranking window and is recorded here as the historical decision rule for how onboarding-timing evidence was intended to move CS-coverage priority.

Purpose

Help readers of current investigation-framework readouts interpret the July 2023 owner-lane arrangement accurately. This is a historical governance note, not a current process guide.

What the July 2023 arrangement was

A working block on July 4, 2023 with Priya, anchored on the prior week's two outcomes:
- The guarded Helio Start plan
- The limited expansion-nudge read that became Expansion Assist

The framing at the time was "same two motions as last week — Helio Start guarded pre-discovery, Expansion Assist behavior-gated." The intent was to distribute who carries each segment so Riley is not the one cutting every segment and rewriting every boundary.

What it established

- Two motion anchors: Helio Start (guarded pre-discovery) and Expansion Assist (behavior-gated).
- A working distribution of segment ownership across the people in the block.
- The principle that a readout should not collapse onto a single author.

What it did not establish

- An approval queue or routing system. The lanes are review lanes, not routing lanes.
- A companywide mandate. The arrangement was scoped to that working block and its two anchors.
- A declaration of maturity, completeness, or board-readiness for any lane.
- The four-production-consumer scope, the source-completeness gate, the day-90 mature-claim windows, or owner certification as a formal step. Those structures were introduced in later kickoffs and briefs; the 2023 arrangement did not authorize them.

tests.request: Create a concise Helio Start decision evidence card for the March 2024 public-product decision. Summarize the readiness cohort evidence across operating volume, support coverage, state integrity, excluded operational cases, and the limits on what the evidence justified. Make the distinction between what the cohort established and what it did not establish explicit. Create it as a new document in the Growth folder.

input.body:
Helio Start — March 2024 public-product decision
Decision evidence card

Scope. This card summarizes the readiness cohort evidence available for the March 2024 decision on whether bounded organic Helio Start should continue on the public pricing page. It is framed as a readiness review, not as a launch, GA, paid-acquisition, or pipeline authorization. The card distinguishes what the cohort established from what it did not establish.

1) Operating volume
- Six mature activation cohorts completed, with 256 of 334 admitted workspaces reaching a valid day-7 first-integration event (76.6% cumulative; per-cohort range 67.6%–79.4%).
- A fixed 50-workspace Helio Start cohort provides an additional read at the cohort level: 39 of 50 day-7 first-integration results are certified (78.0%). This is a single fixed set, not a step to a second batch or to scale.
- Owen's preliminary sixth cohort (as of May 13, 2024): 48 of 60 supported first integrations among admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows (80.0%).
- Launch-day cohort of 34 admitted workspaces: 23 completed a supported first integration within seven days; 11 did not. Routed-before-setup cases remain excluded from the denominator.

2) Support coverage
- Launch-day support load (ordinary setup + permissions/ownership contacts) reported at 29.4 per 100 eligible starts across 34 admitted workspaces. Routed-before-setup cases excluded.
- Fixed 50-workspace cohort (no randomized control): 90th-percentile account-level support effort reached 104 minutes; 7 of 50 workspaces exceeded 90 support minutes.
- Separately, an authority-checklist-exposed cohort (Sep 15 – Oct 31; 45 workspaces, day-90 windows complete) shows a median of 24 minutes, a 90th-percentile of 86 minutes, and 3 of 45 above 90 minutes. That cohort is documented for context; it is not a Helio Start cohort and is not part of the Helio Start readiness set.
- Operating and refusal boundaries held through the readiness window: zero routed-before-setup cases in the Helio Start launch-day cohort; exclusions for migration help in flight, agency-shared or multi-party admin permissions, manual billing exceptions, and heavy support needs at setup remained in force.

3) State integrity
- The day-7 activation window is the validated maturity horizon on file. Day-90 windows are partial: a 52-workspace cohort shows 24 complete and 28 immature windows; a later read reports 40 of 52 complete with 12 immature.
- Across the partial day-90 set, paid-active, canceled-before-day-90, past-due, and billing-hold counts are tracked individually (e.g., 19 paid and active at day 90, 3 canceled, 1 past due, 1 billing hold in one read; 31 paid and active, 5 canceled, 3 past due, 1 billing hold in the 40-of-52 read). These are partial cuts, not final retention rates.
- Exact cohort start and end dates for both sets of admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are not in the source packet and have been requested from Owen (DM slack_dm_1789589233372). Until those dates are supplied, the Helio Start lane remains not board-ready.
- Validation of entitlement and support-state instrumentation has been requested (Daniela); refusal-rule and lifecycle copy are tracked separately (Ines); routed-before-setup path is tracked by Customer Success. None of these checks alters the cohort evidence itself.

4) Excluded operational cases
- Routed-before-setup cases are excluded from activation and support-load denominators by design. This exclusion was not relaxed.
- Migration-in-flight, agency-shared or multi-party admin permissions, manual billing exceptions, and heavy-setup-support needs continue to route out of Helio Start. Assisted-path routing (Customer Success, sales-assisted onboarding) is preserved as the alternative path.
- One applicant needing staff-led CSV mapping or import work for 18,000 contacts was reclassified from accepted to assisted-routed, counted once against the 120-application cohort cap, and never invited through the controlled self-serve path. Entitlement and support states remain singular and current.
- Cohort-level evidence is not combined with v3 evidence, not combined with retained mid-segment or Expansion Assist data, and not combined with paid-source evidence.

5) Limits on what the evidence justified
- The readiness cohort evidence supports a bounded-organic-continuation review only. It does not establish:
  - First-paid conversion as a clean number;
  - Day-90 retention as a final rate (windows are partial);
  - Forecastable revenue or pipeline attribution;
  - Paid acquisition (organic-only boundary through 2026-03-31 stands);
  - A pipeline target or a paid-acquisition target.
- The April 1 paid-traffic rule and separate budget approval rule are unchanged by this evidence. A second qualifying mature cohort and a separate budget decision are still required before any capped paid-acquisition proposal could be considered.
- The fixed 50-workspace Helio Start cohort does not, by itself, support lane closure or a board-readiness declaration, because complete day-90 paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort are not yet available for that set.
- Experimental surface (no concurrent activation/retention + lifecycle + feature-flag experiments during growth-stage reviews) and intake standards are not relaxed.

What the cohort established vs. what it did not establish
- Established: six mature activation cohorts at 76.6% (256/334; per-cohort 67.6%–79.4%); a certified 39-of-50 day-7 read on the fixed cohort; refusal and operating boundaries holding; bounded post-admission support load; preserved routed-before-setup exclusion; preserved organic-only boundary.
- Did not establish: first-paid conversion, day-90 retention, refund-adjusted cash, forecastable revenue, pipeline attribution, paid acquisition, a pipeline target, or board readiness. The lane remains not board-ready pending exact cohort dates and the second qualifying mature cohort.

Evidence freshness note. Source packet dates for both sets of admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows are still pending from Owen; Helio Start reports as organic intake and routing, admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows, supported first integrations, and bounded support load. No pipeline attribution, no paid-acquisition target.

tests.request: Create a concise design-input card for a bounded Expansion Assist proposal before design work begins. Capture the key observed pilot pattern and the evidence limitations that reviewers must preserve. Title it `Expansion Assist — bounded proposal evidence card`.

input.body:
Status: design only. Not authorization to send prompts. Not pipeline, not revenue commitment, not forecast credit.

Lane (boundary to preserve): narrow, behavior-based, state-specific. Active CS adoption or renewal work on an account suppresses the commercial prompt. CS receives a bounded handling list under the five-account weekly cap — not an advance commercial queue.

Observed pilot pattern (descriptive, from two bounded pilots' closed 45-day windows):
- 43 actual exposures produced 13 help-or-options requests and 9 expansions.
- Eligible population: retained-mid accounts only; <=30 accounts; 6x5 stepped-wedge; first exposure week of July 8; observation end mid-September; 5-account weekly handling cap.
- Ceiling-recency rule: the 14-day product-visible usage-ceiling condition was newly required only for the second cohort; 18 of the first pilot's 30 exposures carried an older ceiling event.

Evidence limitations reviewers must preserve:
- No randomized control. The result is descriptive, not causal. Do not re-frame as lift, incrementality, or treatment effect.
- Usage-ceiling evidence alone is too thin without active-admin behavior; the CS-suppression boundary is what keeps the lane narrow, not the ceiling signal in isolation.
- Sample is small (43 exposures). Treat as qualitative input to design, not as a statistical or commitment basis.
- Cohort asymmetry on ceiling recency (first cohort permitted older ceiling events) means cross-cohort pooling overstates comparability.

Proposal guardrails (carry into design work):
- Stepped-wedge rollout, intent-to-treat analysis, assignment-visibility controls.
- Five-account weekly handling cap; CS handling list, not advance commercial queue.
- No pipeline, revenue-commitment, or forecast credit attributed from this wave.

tests.request: Create a concise, current operating checklist for the lifecycle team covering routine-send release, audit and stop conditions, state-changing preflight requirements, and escalation. Use each person's name for routine release, preflight exceptions, customer corrections and incident stops, and engineering release controls. Do not use `you`, `the requester`, or a generic role in place of a person's name. Make the checklist usable without case-by-case approval of each low-risk send.
tests.answer:
LIFECYCLE TEAM OPERATING CHECKLIST
Effective 2028-01-01. Standing authority; no case-by-case approval is required for low-risk routine sends that meet the conditions below.


1. ROUTINE-SEND RELEASE — owner: Ines
   In scope: non-state-changing, educational sends with a clean preflight.
   Standing authority: Ines releases low-risk routine sends within this lane; Riley does not approve each send line-by-line.
   Weekly ceiling: ≤3 routine sends.
   Required preflight, confirmed immediately before release:
     a. No state change since preflight started.
     b. No customer correction, incident, disputed meaning, ambiguity, or exception attached.
     c. No conflicting connector state and no suppression-alias conflict.
     d. Audience, suppression treatment, template output, and release log match the approved send.
   Holds are a designed control, not a defect: 100% of unsupported rows held, 0% released.


2. AUDIT — owner: Ines
   Row-level audit completed within 24 hours of release.
   Audit status visibly open until finished; closed only on completion.
   No further routine release while an audit is overdue and visibly open.


3. STOP CONDITIONS — owner: Riley
   Stop and escalate to Riley immediately on any of:
     - Customer correction identified or required.
     - Incident (live or emerging), including message defect with user impact.
     - Disputed meaning or claim-language concern.
     - State change, ambiguity, exception, or cross-surface issue.
   These auto-stop triggers apply inside Ines's lane as well as outside it.


4. STATE-CHANGING PREFLIGHT

   4a. State-change gate — owner: Riley
       Any send that consumes or changes message state requires Riley's stop-owner sign-off.
       Message-state consumption between preflight and release must be owned and measurable.
       State conflict at any point → fail-closed; release does not proceed.

   4b. Engineering release controls — owner: Daniela
       Daniela retains release, rollback, connector-state, and send-hold control in full.
       Standing fail-closed holds and suppressions remain in force.
       Input-quality issues that produce holds are surfaced to Daniela's engineering team; do not work around them.
       No transfer of release or rollback authority. The three-send weekly ceiling and Ines's lane are not expanded by contract type, message allowance, or send count.


5. ESCALATION ROUTING
   Ines → Daniela: preflight exception, connector-state conflict, suppression-alias conflict, or any hold that exposes an input-quality issue.
   Ines → Riley: any stop-condition hit, ambiguous or disputed send, customer correction, incident, state-changing send, or exception-heavy / out-of-lane request.
   Daniela → Riley: any release or rollback that intersects a customer-correction, incident, or disputed-semantics lane.
   Riley → Priya: any proposal to expand lane boundaries, alter the three-send ceiling, change the 24-hour audit SLA, or revise permanent delegation status.

tests.request: Create a concise one-page document titled `Expansion Assist — 2028 planning claims boundary` for leadership. State what kind of evidence supports the standing lane, what leadership may say, what pipeline, revenue, forecast, and rollout claims remain prohibited, and the status of the old time-based nudge.

input.body:
Expansion Assist — 2028 planning claims boundary
Page 1 of 1 — for leadership

Standing lane. Expansion Assist is the narrow, behavior-based, state-specific retained-mid operating lane approved December 27, 2024 as a standing operating lane (not a one-off cohort, not a broad rollout). It is governed by current-state eligibility (monthly refresh, deeper integration use, a product-visible usage ceiling newly crossed within the prior 14 days, recent activity by a qualifying human admin who remains active at the eligibility check, fail-closed on stale / conflicting / deactivated-admin records) and by active Customer Success suppression (any account with active CS adoption or renewal work at exposure is suppressed). The lane is separate from Helio Start and from the organic pricing-page motion; lifecycle consolidation is not in scope while each has its own read.

Evidence that supports the standing lane. Across the two bounded pilots' closed, complete 45-day outcome windows, the certified extract shows 43 actual exposures, 13 help-or-options requests, and 9 expansions. Every exposure met standing current-state criteria; no account had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work at exposure. The exposures are descriptive operational observations only: no randomized control, no control group, no holdout. The standing lane is supported by these counts and by the eligibility and suppression rules; it is not supported by causal, revenue, or forecast treatment.

What leadership may say. That Expansion Assist is a narrow, behavior-gated, state-specific retained-mid lane with a certified descriptive extract of 43 / 13 / 9 over the two bounded pilots' closed windows; that current-state eligibility and active-CS-suppression remain controlling; that the lane is separate from Helio Start and from the pricing-page motion.

What remains prohibited in 2028 planning.

  - Pipeline: no Expansion Assist exposure, request, or expansion enters any pipeline report, pipeline cover, or pipeline commitment for 2028.
  - Revenue: no Expansion Assist figure is committed as 2028 revenue; no expansion counted against a quota, plan, or booked number.
  - Forecast: no Expansion Assist outcome is credited to the 2028 forecast; the lane does not appear as a Q1–Q4 forecast line, a commit lever, or a cushion item.
  - Rollout: Expansion Assist is not a broad retained-mid rollout; it is not a launch; it is not a replacement for the retired day-60 basis; it is not a Q-item (not Q1, not Q3, not any quarter) in the forecast or the plan.

Status of the old time-based nudge. The old day-60 basis is retired and is not reinstated. Expansion Assist does not replace it, does not extend it, and does not inherit its claims. The descriptive 43 / 13 / 9 extract stands on its own current-state evidence; the retired day-60 artifact is referenced for history only and carries no 2028 planning weight.

input.body:
STATUS: DRAFT — NOT SENT, NOT ACCEPTED. Sam is preparing to include these scheduling protections in a counteroffer to the restaurant. Nothing here has been delivered or agreed to. Use this sheet for household planning and to prep for the counteroffer conversation; do not treat any of it as a settled change.

PROPOSED PROTECTIONS (summary)

1. One fixed no-service evening per week
   - Sam designates one weekday evening each week as a guaranteed no-service evening.
   - The restaurant cannot schedule him for service, prep, or on-call during that evening, including for private events.
   - The specific weekday is NOT listed here on purpose — check the current rota records for which weekday Sam has selected, and confirm before any calendar planning or counteroffer discussion.

2. Protected shared window on that evening
   - Within the protected evening, a fixed block (currently 6:30 pm–9:30 pm) is reserved as household time.
   - No restaurant service, prep, or Helio work during that block.
   - Treat the block as locked on the household calendar; Kibo loop, dinner, and wind-down plan around it.

3. Ordinary rota notice — minimum three weeks
   - The restaurant must post ordinary monthly rotas at least three weeks (21 days) before the rota's first covered date.
   - Rotas posted with less notice do not waive the three-week term — Sam keeps the right to flag short-notice postings (e.g., the May 2025 18-day delivery, the December 2027 20-day delivery, the December 2027 15-day one-off) and ask that future ordinary rotas return to the three-week standard.
   - One-off short-notice shifts due to staffing emergencies are handled case-by-case; they do not become the new baseline.

4. Protected evening is not default event coverage
   - Private dinners, tasting events, or other special services cannot default to the protected evening.
   - If a private event is being scheduled, it must be placed on a non-protected day, or Sam must explicitly and voluntarily agree in advance — silence or rota silence is not consent.
   - Conflicts (e.g., the July 12, 2027 private-dinner service that landed on the protected Monday) are resolved by reassignment, not by changing his role terms.

5. Role-term status
   - These four protections are written into Sam's role agreement, not granted as discretionary exceptions.
   - The counteroffer is asking the restaurant to confirm these terms continue unchanged (and to cure any recent short-notice or protected-evening lapses).
   - Sunday watercolor remains a separate, private anchor for Sam and is unaffected by this counteroffer.

WHAT THE COUNTEROFFER DOES NOT CHANGE
- Sam's authority over seasonal menu development and private dining (effective April 7, 2025) and quarterly profit participation.
- The household's standing rule that the protected weekday and its shared block stay clear on the home calendar.
- The household's separate understanding with Helio: no Helio work bleeds into the protected block.

HOUSEHOLD PLANNING REMINDERS
- Build the weekly plan around the protected evening and its shared block before scheduling anything else.
- If a rota arrives with less than three weeks' notice, log it (date posted, first covered date, days notice) and flag it to Sam — do not assume acceptance waives the term.
- If a private event or extra close appears on or near the protected evening, treat it as a conflict to resolve by reassignment, not by reshaping the household week.
- For the specific protected weekday, always confirm against the current rota records — this sheet intentionally omits the day.

OPEN ITEMS TO CONFIRM BEFORE SAM SENDS
- Exact weekday Sam is designating (cross-check with current rota records).
- Whether the counteroffer also asks for any remedy on recent short-notice postings or just preserves the term going forward.
- Tone/length of the note (concise professional note is the established pattern — see May 2025 and December 2027 examples).
- Whether Sam wants to reference the role-agreement clause numbers or keep the note clause-neutral.

Remember: DRAFT ONLY. No message has gone out. Do not announce protections as agreed until Sam confirms the counteroffer was sent AND the restaurant has accepted in writing.

tests.request: Create a new document titled “Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test — completed metric scorecard.” Summarize the completed experiment in a concise scorecard covering total traffic and arm counts, the routed-out primary result, admission-completion and support-time guardrails, consistency across the weekly and stabilization cohorts, and the concurrent pricing-page change check.

input.body:
Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test — completed metric scorecard

Window: 2025-10-20 → 2025-11-16 (three weekly cohorts + Nov 10–16 stabilization)
Split: organic-only 50/50 on the pricing page; no paid traffic, pipeline, or forecast credit in scope

1. Total traffic and arm counts
- 3,286 organic pricing-page sessions: 1,639 control, 1,647 treatment
- Helio Start eligibility-flow starts: 344 control, 352 treatment

2. Routed-out primary result
- Routed out for an existing unsupported condition: 38/344 control (11.0%) vs 25/352 treatment (7.1%)
- Relative reduction: 35.7% (above the ≥25% threshold)

3. Admission-completion guardrail (limit: ≤1.5 pp decline)
- Eligible-workspace admission completion: 43.8% control vs 44.1% treatment → +0.3 pp, inside limit

4. Support-time guardrail (limit: ≤10 min increase, account-level p90)
- Account-level support time, 90th percentile: 71 min control vs 74 min treatment → +3 min, inside limit

5. Consistency across cohorts
- Weekly cohort 1 (Oct 20–26): 781 sessions (389/392); route-out 9/82 control (11.0%) vs 7/86 treatment (8.1%); admission 43.9% vs 44.2%; support p90 70 vs 73 min
- Weekly cohort 2 (Oct 27–Nov 2): 832 sessions (414/418); route-out 10/87 (11.5%) vs 6/89 (6.7%); admission 43.7% vs 44.0%; support p90 72 vs 75 min
- Weekly cohort 3 (Nov 3–9): 817 sessions (408/409); route-out 9/86 (10.5%) vs 6/88 (6.8%); admission 43.8% vs 44.2%; support p90 71 vs 74 min
- Stabilization cohort (Nov 10–16): favorable direction held; both guardrails stayed inside limits; treatment remained non-default throughout

6. Concurrent pricing-page change check
- Pricing-page layout and UI freeze held through Nov 16, 2025
- No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred during the window
- Clean attribution; no concurrent layout/UI confounders
- No new lifecycle branch, no change to eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, instrumentation, or assisted support-routing rules

    page / forecast signal.

------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------
  [DATE]  [author]  [what changed; which lane(s); gate impact]

tests.request: Create a compact evidence-trajectory memo titled `Expansion nudge evidence trajectory — 2028 planning` in the Growth folder. Trace the experiment from design through the first weekly observation to the final conclusion. Include the early sample limitation, what the team decided to do after that read and for how long, and the final rollout boundary.

input.body:
Experiment: EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge (flag: expansion_nudge_60d_v1)
Owner: Riley (run), Owen (weekly cuts), Ines (copy)
Scope: in-product prompt at day 60, retained mid-seg v2 / 75–200 seat paid accounts only

DESIGN
- Hypothesis: at least +$8 expansion MRR per account.
- Pre-launch proxy: a "dumb squint" scratch cut on 2023-05-07 at 16:14 CT. Sample was baby-sized; treated as sizing only, not a live read, too early to conclude.
- Launch: 2023-05-23, flag flipped from designed → running at 25% rollout, with a 2-week planned read window and an isolation note that explicitly prohibited reading email lift into the experiment.

FIRST WEEKLY OBSERVATION (2023-06-01)
- Treatment ahead by roughly +$4 expansion MRR per account vs control.
- n = 92.
- PostHog slice matched the warehouse; result logged.
- Below the +$8 bar, sample too small for statistical significance at p = 0.05.
- Decision: hold off on any shipping decision and let the run continue, expecting two more weeks of data.

MID-RUN READS
- 2023-06-08: Owen's next cut, described as more informative than the n=92 snapshot.
- 2023-06-22: aggregate treatment +$6.10 per account (n=372), still below the +$8 bar. High-depth sub-slice — 3+ integrations by day 45 AND 2+ active admins in the trailing 14 days, n=118 — read at +$13.20. Low-depth slice flat. Owen's read: "behavior-gated, not day-60 gated; would not widen the current flag without a new eligibility model."

EARLY SAMPLE LIMITATION
- n = 92 on 2023-06-01 was under-powered for p = 0.05 and well below the 2-week-read sample target. No shipping signal; treated as data-continuation, not a decision point.

POST-READ DECISION AND DURATION
- Hold the flag at 25% through the full 2-week window plus the follow-on cuts to land an aggregate read; do not widen; do not read email lift into it; ship neither the aggregate nor the high-depth sub-slice into Q3 forecast.

FINAL READ AND CONCLUSION (landed 2023-06-29)
- Aggregate ~+$6.20 per account (n=392, p=0.16) — below the +$8 bar.
- Low-depth slice flat (~$+0.60); high-depth slice +$13.20 (n=118).
- Status: inconclusive as a blanket retained-mid expansion answer.
- Learning carryforward: behavior-based Expansion Assist prompts, scoped to behaviorally eligible accounts only (integration depth + active-admin + product-visible usage ceiling, fail-closed on stale/conflicting data), not yet designed, not yet running.

ROLLOUT BOUNDARY
- expansion_nudge_60d_v1 stays at 25% during the read, then rolled back to 0% (flag status: rolled_back). It is not widened, not blended into Expansion Assist, not used as a Q3 forecast line. Future Expansion Assist work must use a separate behavior-based eligibility model, not this prompt.

tests.request: Create a compact Helio Start public-intake routing reference using the rules approved for the March 2024 launch.

input.body:
# Helio Start — Public Intake Routing Reference
*Approved March 2024 launch rules. Compact field guide for the public pricing-page path.*

## 1. Public path (in)
Limited to under-50 accounts meeting all five conditions:
- Admin proof present
- Deployment simplicity (no migration/import complexity)
- First-week integration fit (connector live in connector-access change)
- Current entitlement state
- Supported billing conditions

## 2. Admit vs. corroborate
- Legitimate domain mismatches → admit only with corroborating evidence (admin proof + matched billing or deployment evidence).
- Missing corroboration → route out.

## 3. Route out
- Agency identities
- Manual billing
- Imports / migrations
- Unsupported permissions
- Any account >50 seats
- Any account missing admin proof, entitlement, or supported billing without corroboration

## 4. Prompt-hold rule
If a case matches an approved authority pattern but arrives via an unapproved surface, hold the prompt and escalate — do not auto-respond.

## 5. Separate reporting
Helio Start reporting stays separate from retained mid-segment and Expansion Assist. No paid-acquisition or pipeline target on this path.
